final_roohangiz_saminejad.clue_text: Playing the heroine Golnar in the سال ۱۳۱۲ خورشیدی pioneering sound film Dokhtar-e Lor, this woman made history as the first Iranian female actress to speak and appear unveiled on celluloid.
final_roohangiz_saminejad.explanation: Saminejad faced severe family ostracism and harassment in conservative Tehran after the premiere, living in seclusion under an assumed name until her death در سال ۱۳۷۶ خورشیدی.

final_strangling_of_persia_book.clue_text: Upon being expelled by Russian troops in آذر ۱۲۹۰, Treasurer-General Morgan Shuster published this international bestseller exposing the destruction of Iranian democracy.
final_strangling_of_persia_book.explanation: Shuster's book opened with the memorable line: 'It was the European policy of Russia and Great Britain in Persia to destroy the independence of a nation.'

final_ferdowsi_millenary.clue_text: In مهر ۱۳۱۳, orientalists and scholars from around the world gathered in Tus for this international congress, unveiling Ferdowsi's cubic marble mausoleum.
final_ferdowsi_millenary.explanation: Karim Taherzadeh Behzad designed the mausoleum in Achaemenid stone style, embodying Reza Shah's nationalist renaissance of pre-Islamic architectural heritage.

final_shahnameh_feraydun.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the Shahnameh, this righteous prince united with Kaveh the Blacksmith to overthrow the serpent tyrant Zahhak, chaining him beneath Mount Damavand.
final_shahnameh_feraydun.explanation: Fereydun struck Zahhak with his ox-headed mace (Gorz-e Gavsar), establishing the ancient autumn festival of Mehregan.

single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.clue_text: در سال ۴۹۰ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, Athenian hoplites under Miltiades repulsed the amphibious landing force of Darius the Great on this coastal plain 26 miles northeast of Athens.
single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.explanation: The defeat marked the first time an Achaemenid imperial invasion force was repulsed on the Greek mainland, giving rise to the modern marathon race.

single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.clue_text: در سال ۴۸۰ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, Xerxes I's army was delayed at this narrow coastal pass by Spartan King Leonidas and his 300 hoplites before an encircling goat path was revealed.
single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.explanation: After a local Greek named Ephialtes showed the Persians the Anopaia mountain path, the Immortals outflanked the Greeks, allowing Xerxes to advance on Athens.

single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Watching from a golden throne atop Mount Aigaleo, Xerxes saw his vast Phoenician and Persian armada outmaneuvered and destroyed by Greek triremes in this strait.
single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.explanation: Themistocles lured the Persian fleet into narrow waters where their numerical advantage was negated, compelling Xerxes to withdraw to Asia.

single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.clue_text: در سال ۴۰۱ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, Cyrus the Younger rebelled against his brother Artaxerxes II with 10,000 Greek mercenaries at this battle, immortalized in Xenophon's Anabasis.
single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.explanation: Cyrus was killed in the battle; the stranded Greek mercenaries (The Ten Thousand) marched across thousands of miles of hostile Persian territory to reach the Black Sea.

single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.clue_text: در سال ۳۳۰ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, satrap Ariobarzanes and his sister Youtab held this narrow pass in the Zagros Mountains with 700 men, ambushing Alexander the Great's army with avalanches.
single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.explanation: Hailed as the 'Persian Thermopylae', Ariobarzanes fought to the last man until a local shepherd guided Alexander around the pass to Persepolis.

single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the final trial of Rostam's Seven Labors (Haft Khan), Rostam slays this demonic king of Mazandaran inside a dark cavern, using its blood to restore King Kay Kavus's eyesight.
single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.explanation: Rostam cut out the White Demon's liver, dripping its warm bile into the blinded eyes of the captive Iranian knights to restore their sight.

single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This shape-shifting demon transformed into a wild golden zebra, hurled a slumbering Rostam into the Caspian Sea, and possessed the power to turn stone into water.
single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.explanation: When Akvan asked Rostam whether he preferred to be cast into the mountains or the sea, Rostam used reverse psychology, knowing demons always do the opposite.

single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In his third labor, Rostam was awakened in the wilderness three times by his stallion Rakhsh before slaying this colossal venomous monster.
single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.explanation: The eighty-meter dragon made itself invisible whenever Rostam opened his eyes, until Rakhsh trampled it and Rostam severed its head with his ox-head mace.

single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In pre-Islamic Iranian mythology and the Shahnameh, this divine, glowing halo of royal fortune and destiny legitimizes kings and departs when they succumb to hubris.
single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.explanation: King Jamshid lost the divine Farr (Farr-e Izadi) when he boasted that he was greater than God, causing his kingdom to fall to the tyrant Zahhak.

single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This Turanian king is the lifelong arch-nemesis of Iran in the Shahnameh, repeatedly invading the realm and ordering the murder of Prince Siavash.
single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.explanation: Afrasiyab reigned over Turan for centuries through sorcery until captured in Lake Chichast by the hermit Hom and executed by King Kay Khosrow.

single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.clue_text: Born in Shiraz in ۱۵۷۱ and teaching at Khan Madrasa, this supreme philosopher synthesized Avicennian Peripateticism and Suhrawardi's Illuminationism into Transcendent Theosophy.
single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.explanation: Sadr al-Din Mohammad Shirazi (Mulla Sadra) founded Hikmat al-Muta'aliyah, positing the primacy of existence (Asalat al-Wujud) over essence.

single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Considered Mulla Sadra's magnum opus, this massive philosophical treatise in nine volumes takes its title from 'The Four Intellectual Journeys of the Soul'.
single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.explanation: The four journeys trace the soul's path: from creation to God, in God, from God back to creation with God, and among creation to guide humanity.

single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Known as the 'Third Teacher' after Aristotle and Al-Farabi, this eccentric master in Isfahan solved the creation of the universe with his theory of Huduth-e Dahri (At-Temporal Origination).
single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.explanation: Mir Damad was revered by Shah Abbas I, who famously walked beside his horse through the streets of Isfahan to demonstrate royal reverence for philosophy.

single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Born in Baalbek (Lebanon) and brought to Iran as a child, this polymath and architect designed the hydraulic heating of the Sheikh Bahai bathhouse using a single candle.
single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.explanation: Sheikh Baha al-Din al-Amili also engineered the division of the Zayandeh River's waters across the districts of Isfahan (Tomar-e Sheikh Bahai).

single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Compiling the 110-volume hadith encyclopedia Bihar al-Anwar (Oceans of Light), this influential late Safavid cleric suppressed philosophy and Sufism under Shah Sultan Husayn.
single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.explanation: Majlisi's strict clerical legalism marginalized religious minorities and contributed to the social ossification that preceded the Afghan conquest در سال ۱۱۰۱ خورشیدی.

single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_20.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Measuring 1,491 square kilometers in the Strait of Hormuz, this dolphin-shaped island is the largest island in the Persian Gulf, famous for Hara mangrove forests.
single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_20.explanation: Qeshm features the UNESCO Global Geopark, the Stars Valley (Darreh-ye Setaregan), and the Chahkooh Gorge carved by erosion.

single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_40.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Transformed in the 1970s into a duty-free luxury haven with a Grand Casino and supersonic Concorde flights, this 91-square-kilometer coral island lies in the Persian Gulf.
single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_40.explanation: Kish remains a major visa-free shopping and tourism free-trade zone, famous for the scenic wreck of the Greek Cargo Ship grounded on its coral reefs در سال ۱۳۴۵ خورشیدی.

single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_60.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Handling over ninety percent of all Iranian crude oil exports via deepwater sea berths, this fortified rocky island was bombed over 2,800 times by Iraqi jets during the war.
single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_60.explanation: Kharg Island was shielded by Hawk anti-aircraft missile batteries and heroic repair crews who kept oil pumping onto tankers throughout the eight-year Tanker War.

single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_80.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Renowned for its red ochre beaches and rainbow-colored salt canyons, this tiny island features the ruins of an imposing 16th-century fortress built by Afonso de Albuquerque.
single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_80.explanation: Hormuz Island was the commercial pearl of the Indies until Safavid commander Imam Quli Khan expelled the Portuguese garrison در سال ۱۰۰۱ خورشیدی.

single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_10.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Originally named Gombroon and developed into Iran's primary container shipping port by Shah Abbas I, this coastal metropolis looks out over the Strait of Hormuz.
single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_10.explanation: Home to the Shahid Rajaee container terminal, Bandar Abbas handles over half of Iran's maritime sea trade today.

single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: A towering playwright and director of Death of Yazdgerd and Bashu, the Little Stranger, this auteur is the grandmaster of historical allegorical theatre and film.
single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.explanation: Beyzai's research into pre-Islamic dramatic traditions culminated in his monumental book A Study of Iranian Theatre (سال ۱۳۴۳ خورشیدی).

single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Known as the 'poet of Iranian cinema' for his lyrical historical dialogues, this director created the immortal TV epic Hezar Dastan and the beloved tearjerker Mother (Madar).
single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.explanation: Hatami built the famous Ghazali Cinema Town in west Tehran to recreate 1930s Lalezar Street and the Tupkhaneh square for his cinematic works.

single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.clue_text: Directing Still Life (سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی) and A Simple Event, this pioneer of international cinematic minimalism emigrated to Germany and inspired directors like Chantal Akerman and Jim Jarmusch.
single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.explanation: Still Life won the Silver Bear at the سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی Berlin Film Festival, featuring an aging railway switchman told he is being retired after 33 years of routine.

single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.clue_text: Directing A Separation (سال ۱۳۹۰ خورشیدی) and The Salesman (سال ۱۳۹۵ خورشیدی), this contemporary master became the only Iranian director to win two Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film.
single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.explanation: A Separation also made history as the first foreign-language screenplay nominated for Best Original Screenplay at the Oscars.

single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.clue_text: This director won the Golden Leopard at Locarno for The Mirror (سال ۱۳۷۶ خورشیدی) and the Golden Bear at Berlin for Taxi (سال ۱۳۹۴ خورشیدی), despite being sentenced to a 20-year ban on filmmaking.
single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.explanation: Panahi smuggled his film This Is Not a Film (سال ۱۳۹۰ خورشیدی) to the Cannes Film Festival hidden inside a USB flash drive baked inside a birthday cake.

single_music_radif_and_dastgah_200.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Persian classical music is organized into this comprehensive canon of melodic motifs (Goushehs), arranged across seven primary modal systems (Dastgahs).
single_music_radif_and_dastgah_200.explanation: Preserved by 19th-century court masters Mirza Abdollah and Aqa Hossein-Qoli, the Radif was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage در سال ۱۳۸۸ خورشیدی.

single_music_radif_and_dastgah_400.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Revered as the undisputed 'Master' (Ostad) of Persian vocal music, this legendary baritone spent six decades mesmerizing millions with his breathtaking Tahrir vocal ornamentation.
single_music_radif_and_dastgah_400.explanation: Shajarian's unaccompanied prayer 'Rabbana' was broadcast at sundown every Ramadan on Iranian radio for thirty years, becoming a sacred national soundscape.

single_music_radif_and_dastgah_600.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Held vertically and played by directing air between the upper incisors and the tongue (Dandan technique), this end-blown reed flute was played with peerless virtuosity by Hasan Kasaei.
single_music_radif_and_dastgah_600.explanation: The Ney opens Rumi's Masnavi with the immortal lament: 'Beshno az ney chon hekayat mikonad' (Listen to the reed as it tells its tale of separation).

single_music_radif_and_dastgah_800.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Featuring a waist carved from solid mulberry wood covered in lamb fetus skin, this premier 25-fret long-necked lute is played with a brass plectrum encased in bee's wax.
single_music_radif_and_dastgah_800.explanation: Renowned luthiers like Yahya of Isfahan in the early 20th century carved instruments whose resonance remains the gold standard in Iranian music.

single_music_radif_and_dastgah_1000.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Featuring 72 strings arranged in courses of four over 18 movable bridges, this trapezoidal wooden hammered dulcimer was brought to modern perfection by Ostad Faramarz Payvar.
single_music_radif_and_dastgah_1000.explanation: The Santur is played using two delicate featherweight wooden hammers (mezrab), producing a crystalline, shimmering soundscape.

single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Grandson of Genghis Khan who sacked Baghdad in 1258, this Mongol ruler founded the Ilkhanate dynasty in Iran and established his capital at Tabriz and Maragheh.
single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.explanation: Hulagu embraced Persian culture and was persuaded by his astronomer vizier Nasir al-Din al-Tusi to construct the Maragheh Observatory in 1259.

single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Serving as Ilkhanid vizier to Ghazan Khan, this Jewish convert physician wrote Jami al-Tawarikh (Compendium of Chronicles), the world's first true universal history.
single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.explanation: Rashid al-Din built the Rab'-e Rashidi academy complex in Tabriz, employing hundreds of scholars, paper makers, and calligraphers to copy his historical manuscripts.

single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Founded in 1259 in Azerbaijan under Nasir al-Din al-Tusi, this astronomical observatory developed the 'Tusi-couple' geometrical model later utilized by Nicolaus Copernicus.
single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.explanation: Maragheh's 400,000-manuscript library and four-meter sextant produced the Zij-i Ilkhani planetary tables that circulated from China to Renaissance Italy.

single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Reigning from Samarkand, this astronomer-prince and grandson of Timur accurately calculated the sidereal year to within 25 seconds of modern measurements before being assassinated by his son.
single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.explanation: Ulugh Beg's star catalogue Zij-i Sultani (1437) mapped 1,018 stars, honored today by a crater on the Moon bearing his name.

single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Completed in 1430 for Timur's grandson Prince Baysunghur in Herat, this illustrated manuscript is universally revered as the supreme masterpiece of Persian miniature art.
single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.explanation: Inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register, its 21 surviving miniatures and calligraphy represent the zenith of the Timurid Herat School.

single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_200.clue_text: In اسفند/فروردین ۱۲۶۹, Nasir al-Din Shah granted this British major an exclusive 50-year worldwide monopoly over the production, sale, and export of all Iranian tobacco.
single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_200.explanation: Talbot paid £15,000 in personal bribes to Prime Minister Amin al-Soltan and promised £15,000 annually to the Shah plus a quarter of net profits.

single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_400.clue_text: Living in exile in Samarra (Iraq), this supreme Marja-e Taqlid issued the historic آذر ۱۲۷۰ fatwa that made smoking water-pipes equivalent to war against the Hidden Imam.
single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_400.explanation: The brief two-sentence fatwa spread by telegraph across Iran, uniting secular modernists, merchant guilds, and the clergy in the first successful mass civil disobedience movement.

single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_600.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Inside the royal palace harem, this favorite wife of Nasir al-Din Shah led his wives and concubines in smashing their crystal water-pipes (qalyan) in defiance of the sovereign.
single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_600.explanation: When the Shah asked who had forbidden smoking in his own palace, Anis al-Dowleh famously answered: 'The same one who made me lawful (halal) unto you.'

single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_800.clue_text: This fiery pan-Islamic activist wrote an urgent letter to Mirza Shirazi from Basra در سال ۱۲۷۰ خورشیدی detailing the betrayal of Iranian sovereignty before being expelled from Iran.
single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_800.explanation: Afghani had taken bast at Shah Abdol-Azim در سال ۱۲۶۹ خورشیدی before being dragged through snow by royal guards and dumped at the Ottoman frontier.

single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_100.clue_text: To cancel the Talbot concession in دی/بهمن ۱۲۷۰, the bankrupt Qajar state was forced to pay this enormous indemnity of £500,000, creating Iran's first foreign national debt.
single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_100.explanation: The British-owned Imperial Bank of Persia lent the funds at 6% interest, secured against the customs revenues of the Persian Gulf ports.

double_provisional_regime_1979_400.clue_text: A close medical aide to Khomeini in Neauphle-le-Château, this American-educated cancer researcher served as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister in the سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی provisional government.
double_provisional_regime_1979_400.explanation: Yazdi and Bazargan met US National Security Advisor Zbigniew Brzezinski in Algiers on November 1, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, triggering the embassy takeover three days later.

double_provisional_regime_1979_800.clue_text: Head of National Iranian Radio and Television and later Foreign Minister, this charismatic aide to Khomeini was executed by firing squad in Evin در سال ۱۳۶۱ خورشیدی for plotting to shell Jamaran.
double_provisional_regime_1979_800.explanation: Ghotbzadeh was implicated alongside Grand Ayatollah Shariatmadari in an army plot to assassinate Khomeini and bomb the clerical leadership in Jamaran.

double_provisional_regime_1979_1200.clue_text: Elected with 76% of the vote in دی/بهمن ۱۳۵۹, this Sorbonne economist wore simple civilian suits but was impeached by the Majles in خرداد ۱۳۵۹ and disguised himself to flee to Paris.
double_provisional_regime_1979_1200.explanation: Banisadr allied with Massoud Rajavi's MEK against the Islamic Republic Party; after his impeachment, the MEK launched a campaign of assassinations that killed hundreds of leaders.

double_provisional_regime_1979_1600.clue_text: Sprouting in mosques across every neighborhood in بهمن ۱۳۵۷, these armed local revolutionary councils seized weapons, policed streets, and arrested former royalist officials.
double_provisional_regime_1979_1600.explanation: Headed by Ayatollah Mahdavi Kani, the Komitehs of the Islamic Revolution functioned as autonomous neighborhood fiefdoms until merged into the Law Enforcement Force (NAJA) در سال ۱۳۷۰ خورشیدی.

double_provisional_regime_1979_2000.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Serving as Secretary of the Revolutionary Council and later Majles Speaker and President, this pragmatist cleric from Rafsanjan was the central kingmaker of the new regime.
double_provisional_regime_1979_2000.explanation: Rafsanjani survived an assassination attempt by the Forqan group in اردیبهشت ۱۳۵۷ and served as commander-in-chief of the war effort from سال ۱۳۶۷ خورشیدی.

double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_40.clue_text: به دنبال مهر ۱۳۵۲ Arab-Israeli War, the Shah led OPEC at the Tehran meeting to quadruple oil prices from $3 to nearly this benchmark price per barrel.
double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_40.explanation: Iran's petroleum revenues rocketed overnight from $5 billion در سال ۱۳۵۲ خورشیدی to over $20 billion در سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی, fueling the Shah's dream of creating the 'Great Civilization' (Tamaddon-e Bozorg).

double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_80.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Heading the Plan and Budget Organization, this Harvard-trained prince resigned after warning the Shah that pumping petrodollars into the economy would trigger runaway inflation.
double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_80.explanation: At the مرداد ۱۳۵۳ Ramsar conference, the Shah overruled economic planners and doubled the Fifth Plan budget, causing port congestion, cement shortages, and 30% inflation.

monument_persepolis_400_encore.clue_text: Begun around ۵۱۸ پیش از میلاد by Darius the Great on a massive stone terrace, this ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire is known in Persian as Takht-e Jamshid.
monument_persepolis_400_encore.explanation: Persepolis featured the monumental Gate of All Nations, the 100-Column Hall, and the Apadana Palace, where delegations from 23 nations brought tribute for Nowruz.

monument_pasargadae_800_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Consisting of a simple gabled limestone chamber atop a six-tiered stone plinth, this austere monument in Fars marks the final resting place of Cyrus the Great.
monument_pasargadae_800_encore.explanation: Alexander the Great reportedly visited the tomb in ۳۳۰ پیش از میلاد, ordering it repaired after reading the epitaph: 'O man, I am Cyrus, who founded the Persian Empire; begrudge me not therefore this little earth that covers my body.'

monument_azadi_tower_1200_encore.clue_text: Inaugurated در سال ۱۳۵۰ خورشیدی as the Shahyad Tower to mark the monarchy's 2,500th anniversary, this Tehran landmark combining Sasanian and Islamic arches was designed by 24-year-old architect Hossein Amanat.
monument_azadi_tower_1200_encore.explanation: Constructed from 25,000 blocks of white Isfahan marble, the monument was renamed Borj-e Azadi (Freedom Tower) after the massive demonstrations of the سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی Revolution filled the square.

monument_fin_garden_1600_encore.clue_text: Completed in ۱۵۹۰ under Shah Abbas, this quintessential Persian paradise garden in Kashan features natural turquoise spring fountains and the bathhouse where Amir Kabir was assassinated.
monument_fin_garden_1600_encore.explanation: Bagh-e Fin harnesses natural water pressure from the Soleymaniyeh Spring without mechanical pumps; in its hammam, royal assassins severed Amir Kabir's veins on January 10, سال ۱۲۳۰ خورشیدی.

monument_soltaniyeh_2000_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Built between 1302 and 1312 by Mongol Ilkhan Öljaitü in Zanjan province, this 49-meter turquoise-domed octagonal mausoleum is one of the world's oldest double-shelled brick domes, pre-dating Florence Cathedral.
monument_soltaniyeh_2000_encore.explanation: The Dome of Soltaniyeh is an engineering marvel weighing 200 tons, whose double-shell design inspired Filippo Brunelleschi in his design of the Duomo of Florence.

ideas_shariati_400_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Lecturing to thousands of students at Tehran's Husseiniyeh Ershad, this Sorbonne-educated sociologist energized revolutionary youth by contrasting dynamic 'Red Shi'ism' with passive 'Black Shi'ism'.
ideas_shariati_400_encore.explanation: Dr. Ali Shariati (سال ۱۳۱۲ خورشیدی–سال ۱۳۵۶ خورشیدی) fused Marxist liberation theology with Shi'i martyrdom symbolism, turning Imam Hussein into a revolutionary archetype for the anti-monarchical struggle.

ideas_gharbzadegi_800_encore.clue_text: In a searing سال ۱۳۴۱ خورشیدی polemic that likened Western cultural and economic consumerism to a cholera outbreak or pestilence, Jalal Al-e Ahmad coined this Persian term.
ideas_gharbzadegi_800_encore.explanation: In Gharbzadegi (Plagued by the West), Al-e Ahmad argued that Iran was like a wheat stalk infested by weevils, mindlessly consuming Western gadgets while abandoning its cultural soul.

ideas_dehkhoda_1200_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Beyond his revolutionary satire, this constitutionalist spent forty-five years compiling the monumental Loghatnameh, the most comprehensive dictionary of the Persian language.
ideas_dehkhoda_1200_encore.explanation: Dehkhoda's Loghatnameh spans over 26,000 pages across 50 volumes, documenting millions of citations, vocabulary, and historical biographies.

ideas_kasravi_1600_encore.clue_text: This outspoken secular historian of the Constitutional Revolution was assassinated inside a Tehran courtroom در سال ۱۳۲۵ خورشیدی by the fundamentalist group Fadayan-e Islam.
ideas_kasravi_1600_encore.explanation: Ahmad Kasravi was on trial for 'slander of Islam' when brothers from Navvab Safavi's Fadayan-e Islam stabbed and shot him and his secretary inside the Palace of Justice.

ideas_faramoushkhaneh_2000_encore.clue_text: در سال ۱۲۳۷ خورشیدی, Mirza Malkom Khan organized this Masonic-style secret society in Tehran, whose literal Persian name means 'House of Oblivion' or 'House of Forgetfulness'.
ideas_faramoushkhaneh_2000_encore.explanation: Alarmed by reports of subversive republican teachings, Nasir al-Din Shah banned the Faramoushkhaneh in ۱۸۶۱ and exiled Malkom Khan to Baghdad.

cinema_gaav_400_encore.clue_text: Adapted from Gholam-Hossein Sa'edi's short story and starring Ezzatollah Entezami as a grieving villager who becomes his own cow, this سال ۱۳۴۸ خورشیدی Dariush Mehrjui film launched the Iranian New Wave.
cinema_gaav_400_encore.explanation: Smuggled out of Iran to the سال ۱۳۵۰ خورشیدی Venice Film Festival where it won the FIPRESCI Critics' Prize, Gaav was praised even by Ayatollah Khomeini as an example of serious, healthy cinema.

cinema_kanun_800_encore.clue_text: Founded در سال ۱۳۴۳ خورشیدی under Queen Farah's patronage, this Center for the Intellectual Development of Children and Young Adults became the incubator where Abbas Kiarostami directed his first films.
cinema_kanun_800_encore.explanation: Kanun's filmmaking department, founded در سال ۱۳۴۸ خورشیدی, gave directors like Kiarostami, Amir Naderi, and Bahram Beyzai artistic freedom and 35mm equipment without commercial interference.

cinema_taste_of_cherry_1200_encore.clue_text: در سال ۱۳۷۶ خورشیدی, Abbas Kiarostami made history as the first Iranian filmmaker to win the Cannes Palme d'Or for this minimalist drama following a man driving around Tehran's dusty hills seeking someone to bury him.
cinema_taste_of_cherry_1200_encore.explanation: Taste of Cherry tied with Shohei Imamura's The Eel at Cannes; when French actress Catherine Deneuve kissed Kiarostami on the cheek during the awards ceremony, it ignited controversy back in Tehran.

cinema_lor_girl_sound_1600_encore.clue_text: Because Iranian facilities lacked sound recording technology در سال ۱۳۱۲ خورشیدی, Abdolhossein Sepanta travelled to this Indian port city to shoot Dokhtar-e Lor at Ardeshir Irani's Imperial Film Company.
cinema_lor_girl_sound_1600_encore.explanation: Bombay was chosen because Ardeshir Irani had produced Alam Ara (India's first sound feature) there در سال ۱۳۱۰ خورشیدی and welcomed Sepanta to create the first Persian-language sound movie.

cinema_fajr_festival_2000_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Named after the Quranic dawn surah and held annually every February to mark the anniversary of the revolution, this is Iran's highest cinematic award ceremony, presenting the Crystal Simurgh.
cinema_fajr_festival_2000_encore.explanation: Inaugurated در سال ۱۳۶۱ خورشیدی, the Fajr Film Festival's prestigious prize is the Crystal Simurgh (Simorgh-e Bolurin), honoring excellence in directing, performance, and cinematography.

diplo_1907_partition_400_encore.clue_text: Signed in Saint Petersburg without consulting the Iranian government, this سال ۱۲۸۶ خورشیدی treaty between Britain and Russia carved Iran into northern Russian and southeastern British spheres of influence.
diplo_1907_partition_400_encore.explanation: The سال ۱۲۸۶ خورشیدی convention ended the 'Great Game' between the British and Tsarist empires, leaving only a narrow neutral buffer strip across central Iran.

diplo_paris_treaty_800_encore.clue_text: Concluding the Anglo-Persian War in اسفند/فروردین ۱۲۳۶, Nasir al-Din Shah was forced to sign this treaty in the French capital, formally relinquishing all Iranian claims to the city and kingdom of Herat.
diplo_paris_treaty_800_encore.explanation: British forces invaded Bushehr and Kharg Island in ۱۸۵۶ to force Iran out of Herat, ensuring Afghanistan remained a British buffer against Tsarist expansion toward India.

diplo_1919_vosough_1200_encore.clue_text: Lord Curzon drafted this secret مرداد ۱۲۹۸ agreement that would have placed Iran's army and finances under British control, secured by massive secret bribes paid to Prime Minister Vosough al-Dowleh.
diplo_1919_vosough_1200_encore.explanation: Outrage over the 130,000-toman bribe paid to Vosough al-Dowleh caused the Majles to reject the سال ۱۲۹۸ خورشیدی agreement and directly paved the way for Reza Khan's سال ۱۲۹۹ خورشیدی coup.

diplo_capitulations_1964_1600_encore.clue_text: In مهر ۱۳۴۳, the Majles passed a bill granting diplomatic immunity and extraterritorial jurisdiction to this country's military personnel and their families in Iran, triggering Ayatollah Khomeini's deportation.
diplo_capitulations_1964_1600_encore.explanation: Khomeini delivered his furious October 26, سال ۱۳۴۳ خورشیدی speech condemning the bill, crying that the Shah had reduced Iranians to lower status than an American dog; he was arrested and flown to Turkey one week later.

diplo_shuster_1911_2000_encore.clue_text: Hired در سال ۱۲۹۰ خورشیدی by the Majles as Treasurer-General, this defiant American lawyer organized the Treasury Gendarmerie before Tsarist Russia issued an ultimatum sending troops to invade Tehran and expel him.
diplo_shuster_1911_2000_encore.explanation: Upon his forced expulsion, Shuster published the international bestseller 'The Strangling of Persia' (سال ۱۲۹۱ خورشیدی), exposing the brutal Anglo-Russian strangulation of Iranian constitutional democracy.

geog_damavand_400_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Rising to 5,609 meters in the Alborz mountain range, this snow-capped potentially active stratovolcano is the highest peak in Iran and the highest volcano in Asia.
geog_damavand_400_encore.explanation: Mount Damavand holds a mythic place in Persian literature, celebrated in modern poetry by Mohammad-Taqi Bahar: 'Ey Div-e Sepid-e Pay-dar-band' (O White Demon in Shackles).

geog_karun_800_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Originating in the Zard-Kuh mountains and flowing through Ahvaz into the Arvand Rud, this 950-kilometer waterway is Iran's longest and only navigable river.
geog_karun_800_encore.explanation: در سال ۱۲۶۷ خورشیدی, Nasir al-Din Shah opened the Karun River to international navigation, allowing the British Lynch Brothers to operate commercial steamship routes into the Iranian interior.

geog_lut_desert_1200_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Famed for its wind-sculpted yardangs (Kaluts) and recorded by NASA satellites as having the hottest land surface temperature on Earth (70.7°C), this salt desert lies in southeastern Iran.
geog_lut_desert_1200_encore.explanation: Dasht-e Lut was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site در سال ۱۳۹۵ خورشیدی; its abiotic Gandom Beryan plateau is one of the most hyper-arid zones on the planet.

geog_hormuz_1600_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Measuring only 39 kilometers wide at its narrowest passage between Iran and Oman, this strategic waterway accommodates twenty percent of global petroleum consumption.
geog_hormuz_1600_encore.explanation: Shah Abbas expelled the Portuguese from Hormuz در سال ۱۰۰۱ خورشیدی with English East India Company naval assistance, renaming the mainland port Gombroon as Bandar Abbas.

geog_urmia_2000_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Once the second largest hypersaline lake in the world, this vanishing body of water between East and West Azerbaijan provinces is home to endemic Artemia brine shrimp.
geog_urmia_2000_encore.explanation: Dam construction, excessive irrigation, and climate change caused Lake Urmia to shrink to less than ten percent of its former surface area, creating hazardous salt dust storms.

women_tahirih_400_encore.clue_text: At the سال ۱۲۲۷ خورشیدی Badasht conference, this brilliant poet and Babi leader removed her veil before an assembly of shocked men, declaring before her execution: 'You can kill me as soon as you like, but you cannot stop the emancipation of women.'
women_tahirih_400_encore.explanation: Fatemeh Baraghani of Qazvin, conferred the title Tahirih ('The Pure One'), was executed by strangulation in the Ilkhani garden in Tehran در سال ۱۲۳۰ خورشیدی.

women_bibi_khanoom_800_encore.clue_text: در سال ۱۲۷۳ خورشیدی, this satirical writer composed Ma'ayeb al-Rejal (The Vices of Men) in furious response to a patriarchal advice book, and در سال ۱۲۸۶ خورشیدی founded the Dushizegan School, Iran's first girls' school.
women_bibi_khanoom_800_encore.explanation: Bibi Khanoom established Dabestan-e Dushizegan in Tehran در سال ۱۲۸۶ خورشیدی; when religious conservatives attacked it as a brothel, she rallied constitutionalists to protect it.

women_taj_saltaneh_1200_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Daughter of Nasir al-Din Shah, this forward-thinking princess cast aside court confinement to play European piano, write Crowning Anguish (Khaterat), and champion constitutional democracy.
women_taj_saltaneh_1200_encore.explanation: Taj al-Saltaneh's memoirs provide an uncensored look inside the royal harem, deploring dynastic corruption, foreign exploitation, and the subjection of Iranian women.

women_savushun_1600_encore.clue_text: Set in WWII-occupied Shiraz and charting Zari's awakening to resistance به دنبال murder of her husband Yusef, this سال ۱۳۴۸ خورشیدی novel by Simin Daneshvar was the first published by an Iranian woman.
options: Tuba and the Meaning of Night
women_savushun_1600_encore.explanation: Savushun (evoking the ancient mourning rituals for Siavash) became the bestselling novel in modern Iranian history, translated into sixteen languages.

women_parvin_etesami_2000_encore.clue_text: Dying of typhoid در سال ۱۳۲۰ خورشیدی at age 34, this poetess excelled in the didactic dialogue form (Monazereh), using allegorical debates between garlic and onion, or a king and an orphan.
women_parvin_etesami_2000_encore.explanation: Parvin E'tesami's Divan displays mastery of traditional Persian poetic forms to advance trenchant social criticism of poverty, greed, and the hollow vanity of rulers.

final_cyrus_cylinder_encore.clue_text: Discovered in Babylon در سال ۱۲۵۸ خورشیدی by Hormuzd Rassam and acclaimed by the United Nations as a pioneering charter of human rights, this 6th-century BC baked-clay artifact proclaimed the restoration of conquered shrines.
final_cyrus_cylinder_encore.explanation: Issued after Cyrus conquered Babylon in ۵۳۹ پیش از میلاد, it permitted displaced peoples—including the Jewish exiles—to return to their homelands.

final_johannesburg_exile_encore.clue_text: به دنبال شهریور ۱۳۲۰ اشغال ایران توسط متفقین, رضاشاه توسط بریتانیا ناچار به کناره‌گیری شد و درگذشت در تیر ۱۳۲۳ در تبعید در این کلان‌شهر آفریقای جنوبی.
final_johannesburg_exile_encore.explanation: Reza Shah died in a residence on Tenth Avenue in Parktown, Johannesburg; his embalmed body was initially sent to Cairo and later entombed in Rey.

final_air_france_747_encore.clue_text: On ۱۲ بهمن ۱۳۵۷, ending fifteen years in exile, Ayatollah Khomeini flew from Paris to Tehran's Mehrabad Airport aboard a chartered Boeing 747 operated by this national carrier.
final_air_france_747_encore.explanation: During the flight, American journalist Peter Jennings asked Khomeini what he felt returning to Iran after fifteen years; Khomeini's famous single-word reply was: 'Hichi' (Nothing).

final_white_revolution_reforms_encore.clue_text: In دی/بهمن ۱۳۴۲, Mohammad Reza Shah launched this sweeping 19-point program of social and economic modernization, whose primary pillar was land reform breaking up feudal estates.
final_white_revolution_reforms_encore.explanation: Spearheaded by Minister of Agriculture Hasan Arsanjani, the White Revolution redistributed feudal lands to millions of peasants and established the Literacy Corps (Sepah-e Danesh).

coldwar_pishevari_400_encore.clue_text: In آذر ۱۳۲۴, backed by Soviet occupying troops, veteran communist Ja'far Pishevari proclaimed this autonomous regional government in Tabriz.
coldwar_pishevari_400_encore.explanation: The Azerbaijan crisis of سال ۱۳۲۴ خورشیدی–سال ۱۳۲۵ خورشیدی was the first major international confrontation of the Cold War and the first dispute brought before the UN Security Council.

coldwar_qavam_moscow_800_encore.clue_text: In early سال ۱۳۲۵ خورشیدی, this wily veteran prime minister travelled to Moscow to outmaneuver Stalin, offering prospective northern oil concessions in exchange for complete Red Army withdrawal.
coldwar_qavam_moscow_800_encore.explanation: Qavam signed the Qavam-Sadchikov agreement in فروردین ۱۳۲۵; once Soviet troops withdrew, the new Majles overwhelmingly rejected the oil concession, leaving Stalin empty-handed.

coldwar_tudeh_1200_encore.clue_text: Founded in مهر ۱۳۲۰ by prominent leftist intellectuals known as the 'Fifty-Three', this pro-Soviet communist party became the best-organized political force in modern Iran.
coldwar_tudeh_1200_encore.explanation: The Tudeh Party ('Party of the Masses') built formidable labor unions among Khuzestan oil workers and railway men, as well as an extensive clandestine military officer network.

coldwar_mahabad_1600_encore.clue_text: Proclaimed in دی/بهمن ۱۳۲۵ in Chahar Cheragh Square by Qazi Muhammad, this short-lived Soviet-sponsored Kurdish republic was defended by peshmerga under Mulla Mustafa Barzani.
coldwar_mahabad_1600_encore.explanation: The Republic of Mahabad lasted barely eleven months; after the Iranian army re-entered the region in آذر ۱۳۲۵, Qazi Muhammad was publicly hanged in Chahar Cheragh Square.

coldwar_cento_2000_encore.clue_text: Signed در سال ۱۳۳۴ خورشیدی as the Baghdad Pact and renamed CENTO after the Iraqi revolution, this Western-backed military alliance anchored Iran with Turkey, Pakistan, and Britain as a 'Northern Tier' shield.
coldwar_cento_2000_encore.explanation: CENTO headquarters moved to Ankara در سال ۱۳۳۷ خورشیدی after the regicide of King Faisal II in Baghdad; Iran remained a member until withdrawal به دنبال سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی Revolution.

single_golden_age_islamic_sciences_200_e.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Known in the West as Avicenna, this 11th-century polymath from Bukhara authored The Canon of Medicine, which remained the standard medical textbook in Europe for five centuries.
single_golden_age_islamic_sciences_200_e.explanation: Ibn Sina (980–سال ۴۱۶ خورشیدی) synthesized Galenic and Aristotelian medicine in the five-volume Canon of Medicine (Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb).

single_golden_age_islamic_sciences_400_e.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Born in Rayy near modern Tehran, this 9th-century chemist and clinician was the first to clinically distinguish measles from smallpox and discover medical alcohol.
single_golden_age_islamic_sciences_400_e.explanation: Abu Bakr Mohammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi authored the encyclopedic Kitab al-Hawi (The Comprehensive Book on Medicine).

single_golden_age_islamic_sciences_600_e.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Originating from Khwarazm, this 9th-century mathematician's treatise on balancing equations gave the world the word 'algebra' and introduced Arabic-Hindu numerals to Europe.
single_golden_age_islamic_sciences_600_e.explanation: His book Al-Kitab al-mukhtasar fi hisab al-jabr wal-muqabala gave birth to the terms 'algebra' and 'algorithm'.

single_golden_age_islamic_sciences_800_e.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Accompanying Mahmud of Ghazni on his conquests in the 11th century, this universal genius calculated the radius and circumference of the Earth with 99% accuracy.
single_golden_age_islamic_sciences_800_e.explanation: Abu Rayhan al-Biruni measured the dip of the horizon from a fort in Nandana (modern Pakistan) to compute the Earth's radius within 16 kilometers of modern values.

single_golden_age_islamic_sciences_1000_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: در سال ۴۵۸ خورشیدی, this astronomer and poet led the committee that created the Jalali solar calendar, which remains more astronomically accurate than the Gregorian calendar.
single_golden_age_islamic_sciences_1000_.explanation: Commissioned by Seljuk Sultan Jalal al-Din Malik-Shah, Khayyam calculated the year's length as 365.24219858156 days, an error of just one day every 5,000 years.

single_the_sufi_mystics_200_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Fleeing the Mongol invasion from Balkh to Konya, this 13th-century mystic composed the 25,000-verse Masnavi after meeting the wandering dervish Shams of Tabriz.
single_the_sufi_mystics_200_encore.explanation: Mowlana Jalal al-Din Mohammad Rumi's Masnavi-ye Ma'navi is revered across the Persianate world as 'the Quran in Persian verse'.

single_the_sufi_mystics_400_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: An apothecary by trade who perished during the 1221 Mongol sack of Nishapur, this mystic allegorist wrote The Conference of the Birds (Mantiq al-Tayr).
single_the_sufi_mystics_400_encore.explanation: In Mantiq al-Tayr, thirty birds (Si-morgh) journey through seven valleys in search of their divine king, realizing that they themselves are the Simurgh.

single_the_sufi_mystics_600_encore.clue_text: Executed in Baghdad in ۹۲۲ میلادی for uttering the ecstatic utterance 'Ana al-Haqq' (I am the Truth), this mystic became the supreme martyr of Persian Sufism.
single_the_sufi_mystics_600_encore.explanation: Hallaj's declaration was interpreted by orthodox jurists as a claim to divinity, but Sufis saw it as the ultimate extinction of ego (fana) in God.

single_the_sufi_mystics_800_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This enigmatic, wild wandering mystic from Azerbaijan arrived in Konya in 1244, transforming a sober Islamic scholar into the ecstatic poet Rumi.
single_the_sufi_mystics_800_encore.explanation: Shams vanished mysteriously in 1248, likely murdered by jealous disciples; in his grief, Rumi composed the Divan-e Shams-e Tabrizi in his friend's name.

single_the_sufi_mystics_1000_encore.clue_text: Born in Khorasan in ۸۰۴ میلادی, this master introduced the concept of Fana (annihilation of the self in God) and was famous for his ecstatic 'shathiyat' utterances.
single_the_sufi_mystics_1000_encore.explanation: Bayazid's tomb in Bastam (Semnan province) became a major pilgrimage center, inspiring generations of poets with his vision of divine ecstasy.

single_shiraz_roses_and_nightingales_200.clue_text: Completed در سال ۶۳۷ خورشیدی, this rhymed prose masterpiece of moral tales and maxims by Sa'di takes its name from the Persian word for 'rose garden'.
single_shiraz_roses_and_nightingales_200.explanation: Sa'di's Golestan contains the famous poem inscribed at the entrance of the United Nations: 'Human beings are members of a whole, in related creation of one essence and soul.'

single_shiraz_roses_and_nightingales_400.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Built in the late 19th century in Shiraz, this Qajar garden features a majestic central pavilion, sour orange orchards, and a towering 200-year-old weeping cypress called Sarv-e Naz.
single_shiraz_roses_and_nightingales_400.explanation: Bagh-e Eram (Garden of Paradise) was laid out by the Ilkhani paramount chiefs of the Qashqai confederacy before being acquired by the Qavam family of Shiraz.

single_shiraz_roses_and_nightingales_600.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Featuring magnificent stained glass that casts kaleidoscope patterns across Persian carpets each morning, this Shiraz landmark is known as the Pink Mosque.
single_shiraz_roses_and_nightingales_600.explanation: Built between سال ۱۲۵۵ خورشیدی and سال ۱۲۶۷ خورشیدی by order of Qajar aristocrat Mirza Hasan Ali Nasir al-Mulk, its extensive pink ceramic rose tiles give it the moniker 'The Pink Mosque'.

single_shiraz_roses_and_nightingales_800.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Containing the tomb of Mir Sayyed Ahmad, brother of the Eighth Imam Reza, this holy shrine in Shiraz is famous for interior walls covered in millions of cut mirrors.
single_shiraz_roses_and_nightingales_800.explanation: Shah Cheragh ('King of the Light') was given its moniker when queen Tashi Khatun built its great dome in the 14th century after a glowing light reportedly marked the martyr's grave.

single_shiraz_roses_and_nightingales_100.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Constructed in the 1760s with 48 solid carved spiral limestone columns and a marble pulpit carved from a single slab, this mosque forms the heart of Karim Khan Zand's complex.
single_shiraz_roses_and_nightingales_100.explanation: The Vakil Mosque's 14-step minbar was hewn from solid green marble transported all the way from Maragheh in Azerbaijan by order of the Regent.

single_tehran_bazaar_to_megapolis_200_en.clue_text: در سال ۱۱۶۵ خورشیدی, after crushing rival khans, this eunuch founder of the Qajar dynasty proclaimed Tehran the official capital of Iran due to its proximity to his tribal base in Mazandaran.
single_tehran_bazaar_to_megapolis_200_en.explanation: Agha Mohammad Khan was crowned Shah in Tehran در سال ۱۱۷۵ خورشیدی; at the time, Tehran was a fortified town of barely twenty thousand inhabitants surrounded by mud walls and watchtowers.

single_tehran_bazaar_to_megapolis_400_en.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Featuring the Marble Throne (Takht-e Marmar) and the brilliant Hall of Mirrors (Talar-e Ayeneh), this historic royal walled complex in central Tehran is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
single_tehran_bazaar_to_megapolis_400_en.explanation: Golestan Palace was the seat of Qajar power; در سال ۱۳۰۴ خورشیدی, Reza Shah's coronation took place in its halls, as did the coronation of Mohammad Reza Shah در سال ۱۳۴۶ خورشیدی.

single_tehran_bazaar_to_megapolis_600_en.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Stretching over 18 kilometers from the central railway station north to Tajrish Square, this tree-lined thoroughfare is the longest street in the Middle East.
single_tehran_bazaar_to_megapolis_600_en.explanation: Constructed by order of Reza Shah in the 1930s to link the central marble palaces to his summer palace at Sa'dabad, it was originally named Pahlavi Avenue.

single_tehran_bazaar_to_megapolis_800_en.clue_text: Completed در سال ۱۳۸۶ خورشیدی standing 435 meters tall, this telecommunications tower overlooking northwest Tehran is the sixth-tallest tower in the world.
single_tehran_bazaar_to_megapolis_800_en.explanation: Designed by architect Mohammad Reza Hafezi, Borj-e Milad features an octagonal pod with a revolving restaurant and observation deck offering panoramic views of the Alborz.

single_tehran_bazaar_to_megapolis_1000_e.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Located south of modern Tehran, this ancient city was mentioned in the Avesta as Rhaga and was the birthplace of Harun al-Rashid before being pulverized by the Mongols in 1220.
single_tehran_bazaar_to_megapolis_1000_e.explanation: After the Mongol obliteration of Rayy, survivors relocated to the small northern neighboring agricultural village of Tehran, initiating its long rise to prominence.

single_sacred_shrines_and_pilgrimage_200.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Located in Mashhad, this sprawling 600,000-square-meter complex is the largest mosque in the world by area, surrounding the tomb of the Eighth Shi'i Imam.
single_sacred_shrines_and_pilgrimage_200.explanation: Administered by the Astan-e Qods Razavi foundation, the shrine complex attracts over 25 million pilgrims annually from across the Islamic world.

single_sacred_shrines_and_pilgrimage_400.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The theological heart of Shi'i clerical training (Hawza) in Iran, this city's gold-domed shrine honors Hazrat Fatima Masumeh, sister of Imam Reza.
single_sacred_shrines_and_pilgrimage_400.explanation: Fatima Masumeh died in Qom in ۸۱۶ میلادی while traveling to visit her brother; her shrine was embellished with golden domes by Safavid and Qajar sovereigns.

single_sacred_shrines_and_pilgrimage_600.clue_text: This shrine in Rey south of Tehran served as the primary sanctuary (bast) where tobacco protesters در سال ۱۲۷۰ خورشیدی, constitutionalists در سال ۱۲۸۴ خورشیدی, and Nasir al-Din Shah's assassin took refuge.
single_sacred_shrines_and_pilgrimage_600.explanation: Nasir al-Din Shah was shot inside the shrine of Shah Abdol-Azim on May 1, سال ۱۲۷۵ خورشیدی, while praying on the eve of his golden jubilee.

single_sacred_shrines_and_pilgrimage_800.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Located near Qom, this mosque has become a massive pilgrimage center due to popular beliefs that the Twelfth Imam (the Mahdi) occasionally appears there.
single_sacred_shrines_and_pilgrimage_800.explanation: Pilgrims drop written petitions into a sacred well (chah-e arizah) behind the mosque, a practice that expanded dramatically during the 2000s.

single_sacred_shrines_and_pilgrimage_100.clue_text: Built in 1418 by the Timurid empress of the same name inside the Imam Reza complex in Mashhad, this architectural jewel was the site of the سال ۱۳۱۴ خورشیدی massacre of anti-hat protesters.
single_sacred_shrines_and_pilgrimage_100.explanation: Empress Goharshad, wife of Shahrukh, commissioned master architect Ghavameddin Shirazi; in تیر ۱۳۱۴, Reza Shah's troops fired machine guns inside, killing hundreds protesting Westernized dress.

single_cuisine_of_the_provinces_200_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Often proclaimed Iran's national dish, this slow-simmered herb stew combines parsley, cilantro, fenugreek, red kidney beans, and intensely sour sun-dried Persian limes (limoo amani).
single_cuisine_of_the_provinces_200_enco.explanation: Ghormeh Sabzi is celebrated for its deep emerald color and savory-sour taste derived from slow-caramelized herbs and dried limes from southern Iran.

single_cuisine_of_the_provinces_400_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Originating in Gilan and served at imperial banquets, this rich sweet-and-sour walnut stew is darkened with concentrated sour pomegranate molasses and slow-braised duck or chicken.
single_cuisine_of_the_provinces_400_enco.explanation: In Caspian cooking, Fesenjan is traditionally made with wild teal duck (morghe-abi), cooked for hours until walnut oils rise to the surface.

single_cuisine_of_the_provinces_600_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Cooked in traditional clay or stone pots (Dizi), this comforting lamb and chickpea broth is separated at the table: the broth is eaten with torn sangak bread, and the solids are pounded into a savory paste.
single_cuisine_of_the_provinces_600_enco.explanation: Eating Abgoosht is an interactive communal ritual involving a special heavy masher called a Goosht-koob to crush the meat, beans, and potatoes.

single_cuisine_of_the_provinces_800_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: From the smoky kitchens of Gilan, this charred eggplant and tomato appetizer is vigorously mashed with abundant garlic and scrambled eggs, named after a Qajar governor of Rasht.
single_cuisine_of_the_provinces_800_enco.explanation: Mirza Qasim Khan Qajar, governor of Rasht under Nasir al-Din Shah, developed the recipe after experimenting in his private kitchen.

single_cuisine_of_the_provinces_1000_enc.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The crowning glory of Persian rice cookery, this golden, crunchy crust formed at the bottom of the pot is fiercely fought over at every family gathering.
single_cuisine_of_the_provinces_1000_enc.explanation: Tahdig ('bottom of the pot') can be made with saffron-infused rice crust, sliced thin potatoes, flat lavash bread, or yogurt layers.

single_traditional_crafts_and_masters_20.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Centered in Isfahan, this exquisite metal art involves fusing vitreous colored enamel onto etched copper dishes and firing them at 800°C to create dazzling azure patterns.
single_traditional_crafts_and_masters_20.explanation: The name derives from Mina (heaven/azure); Isfahani masters like Shokrollah Sanizadeh revived the craft in the 20th century.

single_traditional_crafts_and_masters_40.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Perfected in Shiraz, this delicate marquetry art involves assembling hundreds of thousands of microscopic polygonal rods of camel bone, brass, and rosewood into geometric stars.
single_traditional_crafts_and_masters_40.explanation: A single square centimeter of high-grade Khatam can contain up to 250 micro-elements glued into intricate repeating geometric patterns.

single_traditional_crafts_and_masters_60.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Woven on traditional wooden looms in the desert city of Yazd, this luxurious hand-woven silk and wool brocade cloth often features the iconic Boteh Jegheh (paisley) motif.
single_traditional_crafts_and_masters_60.explanation: Termeh weaving requires immense patience; historical weavers produced barely a few centimeters per day for royal court gowns and ceremonial dowries.

single_traditional_crafts_and_masters_80.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In Isfahan's grand bazaar, the rhythmic clinking of hammers against chisels marks this traditional art of hand-engraving and repoussé on silver, brass, and copper vessels.
single_traditional_crafts_and_masters_80.explanation: Before carving, artisans pour hot melted pitch (Ghir) inside the vessel to absorb hammer blows and prevent the metal from puncturing.

single_traditional_crafts_and_masters_10.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Born in Herat around 1450, this supreme master painter of Persian miniatures revolutionized manuscript illumination with naturalistic movement in the Timurid and Safavid royal ateliers.
single_traditional_crafts_and_masters_10.explanation: Behzad served Sultan Husayn Bayqara in Herat and was appointed director of the royal library in Tabriz by Shah Ismail I in ۱۵۲۲.

double_savak_the_eye_of_the_shah_400_enc.clue_text: Established در سال ۱۳۳۵ خورشیدی with CIA and Mossad technical guidance, this notorious state security and intelligence service watched over every aspect of public life under the late Shah.
double_savak_the_eye_of_the_shah_400_enc.explanation: SAVAK wielded extrajudicial powers of interrogation, surveillance, and press censorship until disbanded by Shapour Bakhtiar in دی/بهمن ۱۳۵۷.

double_savak_the_eye_of_the_shah_800_enc.clue_text: Appointed the first director of SAVAK در سال ۱۳۳۵ خورشیدی, this ambitious general fell out with the Shah, fled to Iraq, and was assassinated در سال ۱۳۴۹ خورشیدی by SAVAK hitmen during a desert hunting trip.
double_savak_the_eye_of_the_shah_800_enc.explanation: Bakhtiar was shot in the Diyala desert in Iraq by a SAVAK double agent who had infiltrated his Iraqi-funded dissident entourage.

double_savak_the_eye_of_the_shah_1200_en.clue_text: Built in the northern foothills of Tehran در سال ۱۳۵۱ خورشیدی, this high-security fortress was designed by German engineers to house political prisoners and armed leftist guerrillas.
double_savak_the_eye_of_the_shah_1200_en.explanation: Evin featured soundproof interrogation cells and solitary confinement wings, becoming the primary symbol of state repression before the revolution.

double_savak_the_eye_of_the_shah_1600_en.clue_text: Heading SAVAK for thirteen years from سال ۱۳۴۳ خورشیدی to سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, this hardline general was arrested by the Shah as a sacrificial concession to protesters, only to be executed after the revolution.
double_savak_the_eye_of_the_shah_1600_en.explanation: Nassiri was executed on the roof of the Refah School on February 15, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, alongside three other imperial generals following summary trials by Sadegh Khalkhali.

double_savak_the_eye_of_the_shah_2000_en.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Located near Tupkhaneh Square in the former Shahrbani lockup, this Joint Committee headquarters was notorious for brutal interrogation of guerrillas.
double_savak_the_eye_of_the_shah_2000_en.explanation: Now preserved as the Ebrat Museum (Museum of Warning), its circular layout prevented prisoners from orienting themselves during interrogation.

double_the_revolutionary_year_1978_400_e.clue_text: On August 19, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, over 400 moviegoers perished when the doors were locked and arsonists set ablaze this cinema in the southern oil city of Abadan, sparking nationwide outrage.
double_the_revolutionary_year_1978_400_e.explanation: The audience was watching Masoud Kimiai's film The Deer (Gavaznha); the public blamed SAVAK, driving millions into active opposition to the monarchy.

double_the_revolutionary_year_1978_800_e.clue_text: On September 8, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی (17 Shahrivar), imperial soldiers opened fire on thousands of unarmed protesters gathered in this eastern Tehran square, an event forever known as Black Friday.
double_the_revolutionary_year_1978_800_e.explanation: Military Governor Gholam-Ali Oveisi declared martial law just hours before troops opened fire in Jaleh Square (now Shohada Square), ending any hope of a negotiated compromise.

double_the_revolutionary_year_1978_1200_.clue_text: On January 7, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, this state newspaper published a libelous editorial under the pseudonym Ahmad Rashidi Motlagh slandering Khomeini, igniting the cycle of 40-day mourning protests.
double_the_revolutionary_year_1978_1200_.explanation: The editorial labeled Khomeini an Indian agent and British pawn, sparking student riots in Qom on January 9 that were fired upon by police.

double_the_revolutionary_year_1978_1600_.clue_text: In مهر ۱۳۵۷, a crippling strike by 37,000 workers in this strategic industry choked off state oil revenues and gasoline supplies, breaking the financial spine of the regime.
double_the_revolutionary_year_1978_1600_.explanation: Oil production plummeted from 6 million barrels per day to barely enough for domestic winter heating, forcing the Shah to impose military rule over the refineries.

double_the_revolutionary_year_1978_2000_.clue_text: On January 16, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, with tears in his eyes at Mehrabad Airport, this monarch boarded his Boeing 707 'Shahin' to depart Iran for an exile from which he would never return.
double_the_revolutionary_year_1978_2000_.explanation: Newspapers famously hit the streets with the iconic massive two-word headline: 'SHAH RAFT' (The Shah Is Gone), triggering ecstatic celebrations across the nation.

single_parthian_arrows_and_shadows_200_e.clue_text: در سال ۵۳ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد at the Battle of Carrhae, this brilliant 30-year-old Parthian general decimated seven Roman legions using mounted horse archers and severed the head of Marcus Licinius Crassus.
single_parthian_arrows_and_shadows_200_e.explanation: Surena utilized the 'Parthian Shot' tactic—feigning retreat while firing arrows backwards over galloping horses—killing 20,000 Romans including Crassus.

single_parthian_arrows_and_shadows_400_e.clue_text: Known as the Great and reigning from 124 to ۹۱ پیش از میلاد, this Parthian king established diplomatic ties with Han Dynasty Emperor Wu of China, officially inaugurating the Silk Road.
single_parthian_arrows_and_shadows_400_e.explanation: Mithridates II revived the Achaemenid title 'King of Kings' (Shahanshah) on his coinage, stabilizing borders from Syria to Central Asia.

single_parthian_arrows_and_shadows_600_e.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This tactical maneuver, made famous by nomadic steppe and Parthian cavalry, involved feigning a panicked retreat before twisting in the saddle to loose arrows backwards.
single_parthian_arrows_and_shadows_600_e.explanation: The maneuver entered the English language as 'a parting shot'—a cutting final remark made upon departure.

single_parthian_arrows_and_shadows_800_e.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Located in modern Turkmenistan near Ashgabat, this fortified royal city was the first capital and ancestral necropolis of the Arsacid Parthian kings.
single_parthian_arrows_and_shadows_800_e.explanation: Excavations at UNESCO-listed Old Nisa uncovered magnificent rhytons (ivory drinking horns) combining Hellenistic craftsmanship with Persian motifs.

single_parthian_arrows_and_shadows_1000_.clue_text: در سال ۳۶ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, this Roman triumvir invaded Parthian territory with 100,000 men seeking to avenge Crassus, but lost a third of his army in a disastrous mountain retreat through Media Atropatene.
single_parthian_arrows_and_shadows_1000_.explanation: King Phraates IV intercepted Antony's 300-wagon siege train at Phraaspa, forcing Antony into a retreat that echoed Xenophon's Anabasis.

single_amir_kabirs_reforms_200_encore.clue_text: Serving as chief minister from سال ۱۲۲۷ خورشیدی to سال ۱۲۳۰ خورشیدی, Amir Kabir founded this pioneering modern polytechnic academy in Tehran to instruct students in engineering, military science, and medicine.
single_amir_kabirs_reforms_200_encore.explanation: Dar al-Fonun opened in آذر ۱۲۳۰ with Austrian instructors, just days before Amir Kabir was executed in Fin Garden.

single_amir_kabirs_reforms_400_encore.clue_text: To inform the public and counter foreign imperial propaganda, Amir Kabir established this first official state newspaper در سال ۱۲۳۰ خورشیدی.
single_amir_kabirs_reforms_400_encore.explanation: Vaqaye-ye Ettefaqiyeh covered domestic administrative news, international world events, and public hygiene instructions.

single_amir_kabirs_reforms_600_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Fighting religious superstition, Amir Kabir launched nationwide compulsory inoculation campaigns against this devastating epidemic disease that routinely blinded and killed children.
single_amir_kabirs_reforms_600_encore.explanation: Amir Kabir weeping over children who died after traditional dervishes told parents vaccination was work of the devil is one of the most famous anecdotes in Iranian history.

single_amir_kabirs_reforms_800_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Amir Kabir slashed the lavish royal pensions and corrupt allowances of this influential group: the Shah's court aristocrats, princes, and imperial harem members.
single_amir_kabirs_reforms_800_encore.explanation: His reduction of royal court pensions made mortal enemies of the Queen Mother (Mahd-e Olia) and Mirza Aqa Khan Nuri, who convinced the Shah to execute him.

single_amir_kabirs_reforms_1000_encore.clue_text: Dismissed in آبان ۱۲۳۰, Amir Kabir was exiled to this central Iranian oasis city before being murdered in its Fin Garden bathhouse.
single_amir_kabirs_reforms_1000_encore.explanation: On January 10, سال ۱۲۳۰ خورشیدی, royal executioner Ali Khan Hajeb al-Dowleh entered the bathhouse and cut his veins while he was bathing.

single_allied_occupation_wwii_200_encore.clue_text: In آذر ۱۳۲۲, Churchill, Roosevelt, and Stalin met at the Soviet Embassy in Tehran for this secret summit code-named Eureka, planning Operation Overlord.
single_allied_occupation_wwii_200_encore.explanation: The Big Three signed the Declaration of the Three Powers Regarding Iran, promising to respect Iranian territorial integrity and independence after the war.

single_allied_occupation_wwii_400_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Because it served as the vital overland corridor transporting millions of tons of American Lend-Lease supplies to the Soviet front, Iran was hailed by this triumphant nickname.
single_allied_occupation_wwii_400_encore.explanation: Over 4 million tons of tanks, planes, fuel, and food were moved along the Trans-Iranian Railway to the Red Army, securing Soviet victory on the Eastern Front.

single_allied_occupation_wwii_600_encore.clue_text: Evacuated from Soviet gulags در سال ۱۳۲۱ خورشیدی under General Władysław Anders, over 120,000 refugees from this European country were sheltered in camps across Tehran and Isfahan.
single_allied_occupation_wwii_600_encore.explanation: Isfahan earned the moniker 'City of Polish Children', where orphanages and schools were established; thousands of Polish graves remain in Doulab cemetery.

single_allied_occupation_wwii_800_encore.clue_text: In آذر ۱۳۲۱, severe food hoarding, currency hyperinflation, and Allied requisition of grain sparked violent riots in Tehran over the shortage of this basic staple.
single_allied_occupation_wwii_800_encore.explanation: Protesters ransacked parliament and looted Prime Minister Ahmad Qavam's house when adulterated sawdust and gravel were discovered in Tehran bakeries.

single_allied_occupation_wwii_1000_encor.clue_text: On August 25, سال ۱۳۲۰ خورشیدی, British and Soviet forces launched a surprise joint invasion of neutral Iran under this British military operation codename.
single_allied_occupation_wwii_1000_encor.explanation: Operation Countenance overwhelmed Iranian resistance in three days, resulting in the forced abdication of Reza Shah and Allied occupation until سال ۱۳۲۵ خورشیدی.

single_modern_prose_and_the_novel_200_en.clue_text: Often hailed as the father of modern Persian short story writing, this diplomat penned the satirical سال ۱۲۹۹ خورشیدی collection Once Upon a Time (Yeki Bud, Yeki Nabud).
single_modern_prose_and_the_novel_200_en.explanation: Jamalzadeh's preface to Yeki Bud, Yeki Nabud was a revolutionary literary manifesto demanding writers abandon flowery court rhetoric for natural vernacular Persian.

single_modern_prose_and_the_novel_400_en.clue_text: Published در سال ۱۳۳۱ خورشیدی while its author was imprisoned as a member of the leftist 'Fifty-Three', this romantic mystery novel centers on the enigmatic painting of a woman titled 'Her Eyes'.
single_modern_prose_and_the_novel_400_en.explanation: Bozorg Alavi's Cheshmhayash follows the detective search for the identity of the dangerous femme fatale painted by revolutionary artist Master Makan.

single_modern_prose_and_the_novel_600_en.clue_text: Chronicling the generational decay of an aristocratic Qajar dynastic family through stream-of-consciousness, this haunting سال ۱۳۴۷ خورشیدی novella was written by Houshang Golshiri.
single_modern_prose_and_the_novel_600_en.explanation: Adapted into an acclaimed سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی film by Bahman Farmanara, Shazdeh Ehtejab is a devastating portrait of inherited cruelty and tuberculosis.

single_modern_prose_and_the_novel_800_en.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Stretching over 2,800 pages in ten volumes, this epic rural masterpiece by Mahmoud Dowlatabadi depicts the tragic struggle of the nomadic Kalmiši family in Khorasan.
single_modern_prose_and_the_novel_800_en.explanation: Kelidar is the second longest novel in world literature, taking Dowlatabadi fifteen years to complete between سال ۱۳۴۹ خورشیدی and سال ۱۳۶۲ خورشیدی.

single_modern_prose_and_the_novel_1000_e.clue_text: Based on a real 1920s incident in Bushehr, this gripping سال ۱۳۴۲ خورشیدی revenge novel by Sadeq Chubak follows Zar Mohammad as he methodically murders the four corrupt notables who defrauded him.
options: The Baboon Whose Buffoon Was Dead
single_modern_prose_and_the_novel_1000_e.explanation: Tangsir was adapted into a celebrated سال ۱۳۵۲ خورشیدی film directed by Amir Naderi, starring Behrouz Vossoughi as the Robin Hood-like avenger Shir Mohammad.

double_clerical_power_maraje_of_najaf_an.clue_text: Serving as sole Marja-e Taqlid until his death در سال ۱۳۴۰ خورشیدی, this conservative grand ayatollah rebuilt the Qom Hawza, avoiding direct political confrontation with the Shah.
double_clerical_power_maraje_of_najaf_an.explanation: Boroujerdi's death in اسفند/فروردین ۱۳۴۰ created a leadership vacuum that allowed the Shah to launch the White Revolution and prompted Khomeini's emergence.

double_clerical_power_maraje_of_najaf_an.clue_text: In Najaf, this supreme Persian Marja issued decisive fatwas supporting the سال ۱۲۸۵ خورشیدی Constitution and declaring that obedience to Mohammad Ali Shah was war against God.
double_clerical_power_maraje_of_najaf_an.explanation: Khorasani mobilized support from Najaf; he died mysteriously in آذر ۱۲۹۰ on the eve of marching at the head of a volunteer army to expel Russian troops from Iran.

double_clerical_power_maraje_of_najaf_an.clue_text: Based in Tabriz, this liberal Grand Ayatollah backed the سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی Revolution but founded the Muslim People's Republic Party to oppose Velayat-e Faqih before being placed under house arrest.
double_clerical_power_maraje_of_najaf_an.explanation: Shariatmadari was stripped of his clerical rank در سال ۱۳۶۱ خورشیدی following allegations of complicity in Sadegh Ghotbzadeh's coup plot, dying under house arrest در سال ۱۳۶۴ خورشیدی.

double_clerical_power_maraje_of_najaf_an.clue_text: Forming an essential alliance with Mosaddegh before acrimoniously breaking with him در سال ۱۳۳۲ خورشیدی, this populist Ayatollah served as Speaker of the 17th Majles.
double_clerical_power_maraje_of_najaf_an.explanation: Kashani feared Mosaddegh's secularism and flirtation with the communist Tudeh Party, welcoming General Zahedi's royalist coup in مرداد ۱۳۳۲.

double_clerical_power_maraje_of_najaf_an.clue_text: Refounding the Qom Seminary در سال ۱۳۰۱ خورشیدی, this Grand Ayatollah protected the seminary through the aggressive secularization of the early Reza Shah years.
double_clerical_power_maraje_of_najaf_an.explanation: Haeri Yazdi adopted strict political neutrality towards Reza Shah, ensuring the survival and financial autonomy of the Qom Hawza as a sanctuary for scholars.

double_the_sacred_defense_battlefields_4.clue_text: Launched in اسفند/فروردین ۱۳۶۱ around Shush and Dezful, this massive joint operation liberated 2,500 square kilometers and routed three Iraqi divisions, paving the way to Khorramshahr.
double_the_sacred_defense_battlefields_4.explanation: Meaning 'Undeniable Victory' from Surah al-Fath, Fath ol-Mobin demonstrated the devastating tactical synergy between regular Artesh armor and volunteer Basij light infantry.

double_the_sacred_defense_battlefields_8.clue_text: In بهمن ۱۳۶۲, Iranian forces launched this daring amphibious assault across the Hawizeh Marshes using small fiberglass boats, capturing the oil-rich Majnoon Islands.
double_the_sacred_defense_battlefields_8.explanation: During Operation Kheibar, Iraq first deployed mustard gas and tabun nerve agent on a massive tactical scale against Iranian troops bogged down in the reeds.

double_the_sacred_defense_battlefields_1.clue_text: In بهمن ۱۳۶۴, Iranian commandos crossed the raging 1,000-meter-wide Arvand River in darkness to capture this strategic oil port on the Persian Gulf in Operation Valfajr-8.
double_the_sacred_defense_battlefields_1.explanation: The capture of Faw cut Iraq off from its coastline on the Persian Gulf and placed Iranian artillery within range of Kuwaiti airfields and oil refineries.

double_the_sacred_defense_battlefields_1.clue_text: Fought in دی/بهمن ۱۳۶۵ in the fortified water obstacles of Fish Lake outside Basra, this meatgrinder battle was the single largest and bloodiest land battle of the war.
double_the_sacred_defense_battlefields_1.explanation: Iran breached three lines of the impregnable Soviet-designed 'Iron Ring' defenses around Basra, but suffered over 20,000 casualties in ferocious artillery barrages.

double_the_sacred_defense_battlefields_2.clue_text: On September 23, سال ۱۳۵۹ خورشیدی, hours after the Iraqi surprise invasion, 140 Iranian Air Force F-4 and F-5 fighter-bombers struck airfields across Iraq in this largest air raid in Iranian history.
double_the_sacred_defense_battlefields_2.explanation: Kaman 99 (Bow 99, referencing Arash the Archer's mythical shot) crippled Iraqi air bases and prevented Saddam from gaining air superiority over Khuzestan.

double_war_literature_and_cinema_400_enc.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Narrated in his distinctive gravelly, poetic voice, this 63-episode television documentary series by Morteza Avini captured front-line frontline soldiers as mystical pilgrims on a sacred path.
double_war_literature_and_cinema_400_enc.explanation: Martyred by a landmine in Fakkeh در سال ۱۳۷۲ خورشیدی, Avini was conferred the official title 'Master of the Martyr Intellectuals' (Seyed-e Shahidan-e Ahl-e Qalam).

double_war_literature_and_cinema_800_enc.clue_text: Directed by Ebrahim Hatamikia در سال ۱۳۷۲ خورشیدی, this emotional drama follows a chemical weapons victim sent to Germany for cornea surgery who encounters his estranged expatriate sister.
double_war_literature_and_cinema_800_enc.explanation: Featuring Majid Entezami's haunting pan-flute score, the film movingly humanized the trauma of 100,000 Iranian victims of Iraqi chemical attacks.

double_war_literature_and_cinema_1200_en.clue_text: Directed by Bahram Beyzai در سال ۱۳۶۴ خورشیدی and shelved for three years, this lyrical anti-war masterpiece follows a dark-skinned boy fleeing southern bombardments who finds refuge with a Gilaki farm woman.
double_war_literature_and_cinema_1200_en.explanation: Starring Susan Taslimi as Na'i-Jan, the film championed linguistic and ethnic unity between Gilakis and southern Khuzestanis despite mutual incomprehension.

double_war_literature_and_cinema_1600_en.clue_text: Narrated by 17-year-old Seyyedeh Zahra Hosseini, this massive سال ۱۳۸۷ خورشیدی bestselling memoir recounts her 20 days washing corpses and defending Khorramshahr during the Iraqi siege.
double_war_literature_and_cinema_1600_en.explanation: Da (meaning 'Mother' in Kurdish and Luri) became the fastest-selling book in post-revolutionary history, running through over 150 print editions.

double_war_literature_and_cinema_2000_en.clue_text: Directed by Amir Naderi در سال ۱۳۶۲ خورشیدی, this iconic New Wave film follows an illiterate orphan named Amiro who survives by shining shoes and collecting ice in the scorched ruins of war-era Abadan.
double_war_literature_and_cinema_2000_en.explanation: The Runner was the first post-revolutionary Iranian film to attract major global acclaim, winning the Golden Montgolfiere at the Three Continents Festival in Nantes.

double_the_white_revolution_in_depth_400.clue_text: Appointed Minister of Agriculture در سال ۱۳۴۰ خورشیدی, this fiery radical lawyer was the intellectual architect of the land reform program that broke the power of feudal landlords.
double_the_white_revolution_in_depth_400.explanation: Arsanjani's radical populism alarmed the Shah, who feared the charismatic minister would eclipse the throne; he was forced out as ambassador to Rome در سال ۱۳۴۲ خورشیدی.

double_the_white_revolution_in_depth_800.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Created under Point Two of the White Revolution, this uniformed corps sent high school graduate conscripts into remote villages to teach rural children how to read and write.
double_the_white_revolution_in_depth_800.explanation: Sepah-e Danesh deployed over 100,000 young men and women into 40,000 villages, dramatically raising national rural literacy rates between سال ۱۳۴۲ خورشیدی and سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی.

double_the_white_revolution_in_depth_120.clue_text: In خرداد ۱۳۴۲ (15 Khordad), bloody riots erupted across Tehran and Qom after the Shah arrested Ayatollah Khomeini for denouncing land reform and this controversial social measure.
double_the_white_revolution_in_depth_120.explanation: Prime Minister Asadollah Alam ordered troops to shoot to kill, crushing the 15 Khordad uprising with hundreds of casualties and solidifying Khomeini's status as the chief dissident.

double_the_white_revolution_in_depth_160.clue_text: Serving as Prime Minister for a record twelve years and six months from سال ۱۳۴۳ خورشیدی to سال ۱۳۵۶ خورشیدی, this pipe-smoking Francophile statesman was famous for his fresh orchid lapel flowers.
double_the_white_revolution_in_depth_160.explanation: Hoveyda presided over Iran's petrodollar economic boom; he was executed on April 7, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, after a summary trial by revolutionary judge Sadegh Khalkhali.

double_the_white_revolution_in_depth_200.clue_text: On March 2, سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی, the Shah dissolved all existing parliamentary political parties, declaring that all citizens must join this newly created single totalitarian party or leave the country.
double_the_white_revolution_in_depth_200.explanation: Rastakhiz ('Resurgence') alienated the traditional bazaar by opening branches to enforce arbitrary price controls, accelerating middle-class participation in the revolution.

double_the_left_in_iran_guerrillas_400_e.clue_text: On February 8, سال ۱۳۵۰ خورشیدی, thirteen young Marxist guerrillas attacked a gendarmerie post in this forested village in Gilan, inaugurating modern armed urban guerrilla warfare in Iran.
double_the_left_in_iran_guerrillas_400_e.explanation: The Siahkal incident led to the formation of the Organization of Iranian People's Fedai Guerrillas (Cherikha-ye Fadai-e Khalq), immortalized in poem and song.

double_the_left_in_iran_guerrillas_800_e.clue_text: The chief theoretician of the Fadayan-e Khalq who wrote Armed Struggle: Both a Strategy and a Tactic, this intellectual was assassinated alongside eight others in Evin در سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی.
double_the_left_in_iran_guerrillas_800_e.explanation: SAVAK officers took Jazani and eight fellow prisoners to the hills behind Evin Prison in فروردین ۱۳۵۳ and machine-gunned them, claiming they had been 'shot while escaping'.

double_the_left_in_iran_guerrillas_1200_.clue_text: During his televised سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی military tribunal, this Marxist poet electrified the country by proudly defending Che Guevara, Karl Marx, and Imam Hussein before refusing to ask for royal clemency.
double_the_left_in_iran_guerrillas_1200_.explanation: Golsorkhi told the military judges: 'I found the first lessons of socialism in Islam and in the life of Imam Hussein.' He was executed on February 18, سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی.

double_the_left_in_iran_guerrillas_1600_.clue_text: Authored by Azeri teacher Samad Behrangi در سال ۱۳۴۷ خورشیدی, this allegorical children's fable about a tiny fish swimming from a stream to the ocean became a banned sacred text for armed rebels.
options: The Old Man and the Sea
double_the_left_in_iran_guerrillas_1600_.explanation: Illustrated by Farshid Mesghali (who won the prestigious Hans Christian Andersen Award), the book warned children that conformity meant death.
