double_the_left_in_iran_guerrillas_2000_.clue_text: Founded در سال ۱۳۴۳ خورشیدی by student intellectuals Hanifnejad, Saadati, and Badizadegan, this armed movement fused Islam with Marxist class analysis before fracturing into rival factions.
double_the_left_in_iran_guerrillas_2000_.explanation: در سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی, a violent Marxist faction assassinated rival leaders and purged the Islamic wing, until Massoud Rajavi rebuilt the organization from inside prison.

double_the_russo_persian_wars_400_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: As Crown Prince and governor of Tabriz, this tragic reformer commanded Iranian forces throughout both wars with Russia, creating the Western-drilled Nezam-e Jadid army.
double_the_russo_persian_wars_400_encore.explanation: Abbas Mirza died of kidney disease in Mashhad در سال ۱۲۱۲ خورشیدی at age 44, never ascending the throne, mourned as Iran's greatest military patriot.

double_the_russo_persian_wars_800_encore.clue_text: Signed in مهر ۱۱۹۲ به دنبال catastrophic rout at the Battle of Aslanduz, this treaty forced Iran to cede Georgia, Dagestan, and northern Azerbaijan to the Russian Empire.
double_the_russo_persian_wars_800_encore.explanation: The Treaty of Golestan also granted Russia the exclusive right to maintain naval warships on the Caspian Sea, turning it into a Russian lake.

double_the_russo_persian_wars_1200_encor.clue_text: In دی/بهمن ۱۲۰۷, مردم خشمگین تهران به سفارت روسیه حمله کرده و این نمایشنامه‌نویس و سفیر مشهور تزار را به قتل رساندند به دلیل پناه دادن به دو زن ارمنی.
double_the_russo_persian_wars_1200_encor.explanation: Griboyedov, author of Woe from Wit, had insisted on strictly enforcing the humiliating terms of Turkmenchay; to avert war, the Shah sent the 88-carat Shah Diamond to Tsar Nicholas I.

double_the_russo_persian_wars_1600_encor.clue_text: Nicknamed 'the Dragon' for his ruthlessness, this Georgian nobleman and Russian commander-in-chief conquered Ganja در سال ۱۱۸۳ خورشیدی before being assassinated outside the gates of Baku در سال ۱۱۸۵ خورشیدی.
double_the_russo_persian_wars_1600_encor.explanation: During parleys outside Baku, Huseyngulu Khan's cousin drew a pistol and shot Tsitsianov; his severed head was dispatched as a trophy to Fath-Ali Shah in Tehran.

double_the_russo_persian_wars_2000_encor.clue_text: On October 31, سال ۱۱۹۱ خورشیدی, Russian forces under General Pyotr Kotlyarevsky staged a night bayonet surprise attack across the Aras River, annihilating Abbas Mirza's camp at this battle.
double_the_russo_persian_wars_2000_encor.explanation: The defeat at Aslanduz destroyed Iran's modernized artillery corps and compelled Fath-Ali Shah to sign the humiliating Treaty of Golestan the following year.

single_the_1971_persepolis_gala_200_enco.clue_text: In مهر ۱۳۵۰, the Shah staged the most lavish party in modern history at Persepolis to celebrate this milestone anniversary of the Persian monarchy.
single_the_1971_persepolis_gala_200_enco.explanation: The 2,500-Year Celebration of the Persian Empire welcomed 60 monarchs, presidents, and heads of state to the ruins of Persepolis.

single_the_1971_persepolis_gala_400_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Catering for the Persepolis gala was entrusted exclusively to this legendary Parisian luxury restaurant, flying 150 chefs and waitstaff to the desert.
single_the_1971_persepolis_gala_400_enco.explanation: Maxim's shut down its Paris restaurant for two weeks to serve peacocks on royal porcelain and 25,000 bottles of vintage سال ۱۳۳۸ خورشیدی Dom Pérignon.

single_the_1971_persepolis_gala_600_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Heads of state stayed in an air-conditioned 'Tent City' arranged in five radiating avenues, custom designed by this prestigious French interior design firm.
single_the_1971_persepolis_gala_600_enco.explanation: Maison Jansen built 50 prefabricated apartment tents draped in French silk and tapestries, each with marble bathrooms and direct international telex.

single_the_1971_persepolis_gala_800_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: At the tomb of Cyrus the Great in Pasargadae, the Shah delivered his famous proclamation opening: 'O Cyrus, King of Kings, rest in peace, for...'
single_the_1971_persepolis_gala_800_enco.explanation: The phrase 'Kourosh bekhab ke ma bidarim' became the defining rhetorical symbol of Pahlavi monarchical continuity with pre-Islamic antiquity.

single_the_1971_persepolis_gala_1000_enc.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: From his exile in Najaf, Ayatollah Khomeini furiously condemned the festival as the 'Celebration of the Devil' in this recorded sermon.
single_the_1971_persepolis_gala_1000_enc.explanation: Khomeini lambasted the $100 million expenditure, crying that Iranians were starving in Fars while European monarchs ate roast peacock.

single_the_trans_iranian_railway_200_enc.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Spanning a deep mountain gorge in the Alborz at an altitude of 2,140 meters, this 110-meter-high masonry arch bridge is the masterpiece of the northern railway line.
single_the_trans_iranian_railway_200_enc.explanation: Constructed by Austrian and Italian master masons under Danish engineering supervisor Jørgen Saxild, Hitler reportedly demanded its demolition during WWII to sever Soviet supply lines.

single_the_trans_iranian_railway_400_enc.clue_text: This Danish engineering consortium was contracted در سال ۱۳۱۲ خورشیدی by Reza Shah to oversee construction of the Trans-Iranian Railway, completing it nine months ahead of schedule.
single_the_trans_iranian_railway_400_enc.explanation: Kampsax divided the mountainous terrain into 43 lots sub-contracted to French, Italian, and Swiss firms, employing up to 55,000 workers at a time.

single_the_trans_iranian_railway_600_enc.clue_text: The northern terminus of the Trans-Iranian Railway was established at this newly created port on the Caspian Sea in Mazandaran, renamed Bandar-e Torkaman در سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی.
single_the_trans_iranian_railway_600_enc.explanation: Bandar-e Shah was connected via rail directly to Bandar-e Shahpur (now Bandar-e Imam Khomeini) on the Persian Gulf.

single_the_trans_iranian_railway_800_enc.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Because trains could not climb the steep mountain gradient directly, engineers designed this breathtaking spiral series of three stacked loops near Gadook pass.
single_the_trans_iranian_railway_800_enc.explanation: A passenger looking out the train window could see the same railway line stacked at three different elevations on the mountainside.

single_the_trans_iranian_railway_1000_en.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: To finance the monumental 1,394-kilometer railway without foreign loans, Minister of Finance Ali-Akbar Davar enacted state monopolies on these two imported household commodities.
single_the_trans_iranian_railway_1000_en.explanation: Passed by the Fifth Majles in اردیبهشت ۱۳۰۴, the sugar and tea monopoly tax ensured complete financial independence from British and Russian banks.

single_tabriz_pivot_of_resistance_200_en.clue_text: Holding the Khiyaban district of Tabriz alongside Sattar Khan during the سال ۱۲۸۷ خورشیدی–سال ۱۲۸۸ خورشیدی Royalist siege, this hero was acclaimed with the title Salar-e Melli (National Leader).
single_tabriz_pivot_of_resistance_200_en.explanation: Baqer Khan was a stonemason and mayor of the Khiyaban quarter whose courage prevented royalist troops under Rahim Khan from crushing the revolution.

single_tabriz_pivot_of_resistance_400_en.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: A young American Presbyterian teacher at the Memorial School in Tabriz, this 24-year-old resigned his post to join the constitutionalists and was shot dead leading a sortie against the siege.
single_tabriz_pivot_of_resistance_400_en.explanation: Baskerville declared: 'The only difference between me and these people is my place of birth, and that is not a big difference.' He was buried as a national martyr in Tabriz.

single_tabriz_pivot_of_resistance_600_en.clue_text: An electrical engineer born in Urmia and trained in Tbilisi, this radical terrorist introduced bomb-making to the revolution and organized the assassination of Premier Atabak-e Azam در سال ۱۲۸۶ خورشیدی.
single_tabriz_pivot_of_resistance_600_en.explanation: Heydar Khan joined the Bolsheviks in Baku and later helped establish the Soviet Republic of Gilan before dying mysteriously در سال ۱۲۹۹ خورشیدی.

single_tabriz_pivot_of_resistance_800_en.clue_text: In آذر ۱۲۹۰, Tsarist Russian troops invaded Tabriz به دنبال Shuster ultimatum, publicly hanging the city's senior cleric on Ashura.
single_tabriz_pivot_of_resistance_800_en.explanation: Mirza Ali Aqa Seqat ol-Eslam was hanged on the sacred day of Ashura for refusing to sign a manifesto claiming the Russian invasion was welcomed by the population.

single_tabriz_pivot_of_resistance_1000_e.clue_text: This brilliant Armenian revolutionary commander led volunteer cavalry from the Caucasus to Rasht and spearheaded the تیر ۱۲۸۸ march that liberated Tehran from Royalist forces.
single_tabriz_pivot_of_resistance_1000_e.explanation: Yeprem Khan was appointed police chief of Tehran after the victory; he was killed in battle against royalist rebels near Hamadan in اردیبهشت ۱۲۹۱.

single_new_wave_poetry_sher_e_now_200_en.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Author of The Garden of Mirrors and Fresh Air (Hava-ye Tazeh), this titan of modern Iranian literature created She'r-e Sepid (White Verse), abandoning all rhyme and classical meter.
single_new_wave_poetry_sher_e_now_200_en.explanation: Writing under the pen-name A. Bamdad, Shamlou translated Lorca and Eluard and compiled the monumental multi-volume folklore encyclopedia Ketab-e Koucheh.

single_new_wave_poetry_sher_e_now_400_en.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: A painter and poet from Kashan who wrote Water's Footfall (Seda-ye Pay-e Ab), his luminous, Zen-like verse opens: 'I am from Kashan, my trade is painting...'
single_new_wave_poetry_sher_e_now_400_en.explanation: Sepehri's Eight Books (Hasht Ketab) synthesized Far Eastern Taoism and Sufi illumination, famous for the line: 'Eyes must be washed; things must be seen differently.'

single_new_wave_poetry_sher_e_now_600_en.clue_text: Writing under the pen-name M. Omid, this master of the Khorasani epic style captured the crushing post-سال ۱۳۳۲ خورشیدی coup depression in his celebrated masterpiece Zemestan (The Winter).
single_new_wave_poetry_sher_e_now_600_en.explanation: Opening with 'They will not answer your greeting; heads are buried in cloaks', Zemestan became the immortal national elegy for the crushed democratic hopes of the Mosaddegh era.

single_new_wave_poetry_sher_e_now_800_en.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Known as the 'Lioness of Iran', this twentieth-century poetess revolutionized the classical ghazal by introducing modern colloquial rhythms and political defiance against tyranny.
single_new_wave_poetry_sher_e_now_800_en.explanation: Nominated twice for the Nobel Prize in Literature, Behbahani penned the defiant anthem 'I Will Rebuild You, My Homeland' (Dobareh misazamet, vatan).

single_new_wave_poetry_sher_e_now_1000_e.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Renowned for his romantic masterpiece Koucheh (The Alley), this beloved 20th-century poet wrote lyrical verse celebrated for its emotional gentleness and accessibility.
single_new_wave_poetry_sher_e_now_1000_e.explanation: Moshiri's poem begins: 'Without you, once again at night, I wandered through that alley...', memorized by generations of Iranians.

double_hostage_crisis_444_days_400_encor.clue_text: On November 4, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, hundreds of radical Islamist university students stormed the US Embassy in Tehran, seizing 52 American diplomats under this official group name.
double_hostage_crisis_444_days_400_encor.explanation: The students claimed the embassy was a 'Den of Spies' (Jasouskhaneh) plotting a repeat of the سال ۱۳۳۲ خورشیدی CIA coup, holding the hostages for 444 days.

double_hostage_crisis_444_days_800_encor.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Serving as the public English-language spokesperson for the student hostage-takers and nicknamed 'Mary' by Western media, this woman later became Iran's first female Vice President.
double_hostage_crisis_444_days_800_encor.explanation: Educated in the United States as a child, Ebtekar later headed the Department of the Environment under Presidents Khatami and Rouhani.

double_hostage_crisis_444_days_1200_enco.clue_text: On April 24, سال ۱۳۵۹ خورشیدی, President Jimmy Carter's military rescue mission Operation Eagle Claw ended in disaster when a helicopter collided with an EC-130 aircraft in this remote desert.
double_hostage_crisis_444_days_1200_enco.explanation: A sudden sandstorm (haboob) blinded US pilots; eight American servicemen died, and the disaster doomed Carter's reelection campaign.

double_hostage_crisis_444_days_1600_enco.clue_text: In protest of the embassy takeover, this veteran statesman and first Prime Minister of the Islamic Republic resigned alongside his entire cabinet on November 6, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی.
double_hostage_crisis_444_days_1600_enco.explanation: Bazargan lamented that his provisional government was 'a knife without a blade' while real power was wielded by Khomeini and the Revolutionary Council.

double_hostage_crisis_444_days_2000_enco.clue_text: Brokered by Algerian diplomats, the 52 American hostages were finally released on January 20, سال ۱۳۵۹ خورشیدی, minutes after this US president concluded his inaugural address.
double_hostage_crisis_444_days_2000_enco.explanation: The Algiers Accords unwove frozen Iranian assets and barred future US military intervention in internal Iranian affairs in exchange for the hostages' release.

final_mirza_reza_kermani_encore.clue_text: On May 1, سال ۱۲۷۵ خورشیدی, on the eve of his golden jubilee, Nasir al-Din Shah was assassinated inside the shrine of Shah Abdol-Azim by this disciple of Jamal al-Din al-Afghani.
final_mirza_reza_kermani_encore.explanation: Mirza Reza was hanged in Tupkhaneh Square in مرداد ۱۲۷۵; his pistol shot ended the 48-year reign of Nasir al-Din Shah.

final_liakhov_bombardment_encore.clue_text: On June 23, سال ۱۲۸۷ خورشیدی, Mohammad Ali Shah ordered the Persian Cossack Brigade under this Russian colonel to bombard the Baharestan parliament building with artillery.
final_liakhov_bombardment_encore.explanation: The shelling of the First Majles initiated the 'Little Autocracy' (Estebdad-e Saghir) that ended when constitutionalist armies took Tehran در سال ۱۲۸۸ خورشیدی.

final_bbc_radio_code_encore.clue_text: At midnight on August 15, سال ۱۳۳۲ خورشیدی, the BBC Persian service signaled to the Shah that London supported the coup by changing its standard sign-on phrase to this exact five-word announcement.
final_bbc_radio_code_encore.explanation: The standard phrase was 'It is now midnight'; adding the word 'exactly' (daqiqan) confirmed Churchill's final authorization to the Shah.

final_dehkhoda_yad_ar_encore.clue_text: به دنبال execution of Sur-e Esrafil co-founder Mirza Jahangir Khan در سال ۱۲۸۷ خورشیدی, Ali-Akbar Dehkhoda penned this immortal elegy opening: 'Remember, of the dead candle, remember!'
final_dehkhoda_yad_ar_encore.canonical_answer: یاد آر ز شمع مرده یاد آر
options: یاد آر ز شمع مرده یاد آر
final_dehkhoda_yad_ar_encore.explanation: Dehkhoda dreamed of Jahangir Khan dressed in white saying: 'Why didn't you say that I died young?', waking in tears to compose the poem in Swiss exile.

final_taq_e_kasra_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Standing 37 meters high near Baghdad, this monumental single-span unreinforced parabolic brick arch was the throne room (Iwan) of Sasanian King Khosrow I.
final_taq_e_kasra_encore.explanation: Celebrated in Arabic and Persian poetry by Khaqani ('Behold the mirror of warning in the Iwan of Mada'in'), it is the largest single-span unreinforced brick vault in the world.

final_khorramshahr_mosque_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Standing as the defiant symbol of resistance throughout the 34-day battle and 575-day Iraqi occupation, this turquoise-domed building was the first landmark visited upon liberation.
final_khorramshahr_mosque_encore.explanation: The mosque served as command headquarters, weapons depot, and hospital; soldiers famously sang Jahanara's mourning song on its steps on ۳ خرداد ۱۳۶۱.

final_arvand_rud_thalweg_encore.clue_text: In the سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی Algiers Accord, the Shah and Saddam Hussein agreed to demarcate the southern international border along this nautical median line of the deepest water channel.
final_arvand_rud_thalweg_encore.explanation: Saddam tore up the Algiers Accord on live Iraqi television in شهریور ۱۳۵۹, citing the river boundary as the primary casus belli for invading Iran.

final_daria_i_noor_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Mounted in an elaborate diamond frame topped by the lion and sun, this pale pink 182-carat table-cut diamond is the sister gem to the Koh-i-Noor in the Central Bank vault.
final_daria_i_noor_encore.explanation: Its name translates to 'Sea of Light'; gemologists believe it was cut from the Great Table Diamond seen by Tavernier in Golconda in ۱۶۴۲.

final_roohangiz_saminejad_encore.clue_text: Playing the heroine Golnar in the سال ۱۳۱۲ خورشیدی pioneering sound film Dokhtar-e Lor, this woman made history as the first Iranian female actress to speak and appear unveiled on celluloid.
final_roohangiz_saminejad_encore.explanation: Saminejad faced severe family ostracism and harassment in conservative Tehran after the premiere, living in seclusion under an assumed name until her death در سال ۱۳۷۶ خورشیدی.

final_strangling_of_persia_book_encore.clue_text: Upon being expelled by Russian troops in آذر ۱۲۹۰, Treasurer-General Morgan Shuster published this international bestseller exposing the destruction of Iranian democracy.
final_strangling_of_persia_book_encore.explanation: Shuster's book opened with the memorable line: 'It was the European policy of Russia and Great Britain in Persia to destroy the independence of a nation.'

final_ferdowsi_millenary_encore.clue_text: In مهر ۱۳۱۳, orientalists and scholars from around the world gathered in Tus for this international congress, unveiling Ferdowsi's cubic marble mausoleum.
final_ferdowsi_millenary_encore.explanation: Karim Taherzadeh Behzad designed the mausoleum in Achaemenid stone style, embodying Reza Shah's nationalist renaissance of pre-Islamic architectural heritage.

final_shahnameh_feraydun_encore.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the Shahnameh, this righteous prince united with Kaveh the Blacksmith to overthrow the serpent tyrant Zahhak, chaining him beneath Mount Damavand.
final_shahnameh_feraydun_encore.explanation: Fereydun struck Zahhak with his ox-headed mace (Gorz-e Gavsar), establishing the ancient autumn festival of Mehregan.

single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.clue_text: در سال ۴۹۰ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, Athenian hoplites under Miltiades repulsed the amphibious landing force of Darius the Great on this coastal plain 26 miles northeast of Athens.
single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.explanation: The defeat marked the first time an Achaemenid imperial invasion force was repulsed on the Greek mainland, giving rise to the modern marathon race.

single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.clue_text: در سال ۴۸۰ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, Xerxes I's army was delayed at this narrow coastal pass by Spartan King Leonidas and his 300 hoplites before an encircling goat path was revealed.
single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.explanation: After a local Greek named Ephialtes showed the Persians the Anopaia mountain path, the Immortals outflanked the Greeks, allowing Xerxes to advance on Athens.

single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Watching from a golden throne atop Mount Aigaleo, Xerxes saw his vast Phoenician and Persian armada outmaneuvered and destroyed by Greek triremes in this strait.
single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.explanation: Themistocles lured the Persian fleet into narrow waters where their numerical advantage was negated, compelling Xerxes to withdraw to Asia.

single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.clue_text: در سال ۴۰۱ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, Cyrus the Younger rebelled against his brother Artaxerxes II with 10,000 Greek mercenaries at this battle, immortalized in Xenophon's Anabasis.
single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.explanation: Cyrus was killed in the battle; the stranded Greek mercenaries (The Ten Thousand) marched across thousands of miles of hostile Persian territory to reach the Black Sea.

single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.clue_text: در سال ۳۳۰ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, satrap Ariobarzanes and his sister Youtab held this narrow pass in the Zagros Mountains with 700 men, ambushing Alexander the Great's army with avalanches.
single_ancient_warfare_empires_at_clash_.explanation: Hailed as the 'Persian Thermopylae', Ariobarzanes fought to the last man until a local shepherd guided Alexander around the pass to Persepolis.

single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the final trial of Rostam's Seven Labors (Haft Khan), Rostam slays this demonic king of Mazandaran inside a dark cavern, using its blood to restore King Kay Kavus's eyesight.
single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.explanation: Rostam cut out the White Demon's liver, dripping its warm bile into the blinded eyes of the captive Iranian knights to restore their sight.

single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This shape-shifting demon transformed into a wild golden zebra, hurled a slumbering Rostam into the Caspian Sea, and possessed the power to turn stone into water.
single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.explanation: When Akvan asked Rostam whether he preferred to be cast into the mountains or the sea, Rostam used reverse psychology, knowing demons always do the opposite.

single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In his third labor, Rostam was awakened in the wilderness three times by his stallion Rakhsh before slaying this colossal venomous monster.
single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.explanation: The eighty-meter dragon made itself invisible whenever Rostam opened his eyes, until Rakhsh trampled it and Rostam severed its head with his ox-head mace.

single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In pre-Islamic Iranian mythology and the Shahnameh, this divine, glowing halo of royal fortune and destiny legitimizes kings and departs when they succumb to hubris.
single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.explanation: King Jamshid lost the divine Farr (Farr-e Izadi) when he boasted that he was greater than God, causing his kingdom to fall to the tyrant Zahhak.

single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This Turanian king is the lifelong arch-nemesis of Iran in the Shahnameh, repeatedly invading the realm and ordering the murder of Prince Siavash.
single_myths_and_monsters_of_the_shahnam.explanation: Afrasiyab reigned over Turan for centuries through sorcery until captured in Lake Chichast by the hermit Hom and executed by King Kay Khosrow.

single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.clue_text: Born in Shiraz in ۱۵۷۱ and teaching at Khan Madrasa, this supreme philosopher synthesized Avicennian Peripateticism and Suhrawardi's Illuminationism into Transcendent Theosophy.
single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.explanation: Sadr al-Din Mohammad Shirazi (Mulla Sadra) founded Hikmat al-Muta'aliyah, positing the primacy of existence (Asalat al-Wujud) over essence.

single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Considered Mulla Sadra's magnum opus, this massive philosophical treatise in nine volumes takes its title from 'The Four Intellectual Journeys of the Soul'.
single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.explanation: The four journeys trace the soul's path: from creation to God, in God, from God back to creation with God, and among creation to guide humanity.

single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Known as the 'Third Teacher' after Aristotle and Al-Farabi, this eccentric master in Isfahan solved the creation of the universe with his theory of Huduth-e Dahri (At-Temporal Origination).
single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.explanation: Mir Damad was revered by Shah Abbas I, who famously walked beside his horse through the streets of Isfahan to demonstrate royal reverence for philosophy.

single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Born in Baalbek (Lebanon) and brought to Iran as a child, this polymath and architect designed the hydraulic heating of the Sheikh Bahai bathhouse using a single candle.
single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.explanation: Sheikh Baha al-Din al-Amili also engineered the division of the Zayandeh River's waters across the districts of Isfahan (Tomar-e Sheikh Bahai).

single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Compiling the 110-volume hadith encyclopedia Bihar al-Anwar (Oceans of Light), this influential late Safavid cleric suppressed philosophy and Sufism under Shah Sultan Husayn.
single_philosophy_of_isfahan_the_metaphy.explanation: Majlisi's strict clerical legalism marginalized religious minorities and contributed to the social ossification that preceded the Afghan conquest در سال ۱۱۰۱ خورشیدی.

single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_20.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Measuring 1,491 square kilometers in the Strait of Hormuz, this dolphin-shaped island is the largest island in the Persian Gulf, famous for Hara mangrove forests.
single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_20.explanation: Qeshm features the UNESCO Global Geopark, the Stars Valley (Darreh-ye Setaregan), and the Chahkooh Gorge carved by erosion.

single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_40.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Transformed in the 1970s into a duty-free luxury haven with a Grand Casino and supersonic Concorde flights, this 91-square-kilometer coral island lies in the Persian Gulf.
single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_40.explanation: Kish remains a major visa-free shopping and tourism free-trade zone, famous for the scenic wreck of the Greek Cargo Ship grounded on its coral reefs در سال ۱۳۴۵ خورشیدی.

single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_60.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Handling over ninety percent of all Iranian crude oil exports via deepwater sea berths, this fortified rocky island was bombed over 2,800 times by Iraqi jets during the war.
single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_60.explanation: Kharg Island was shielded by Hawk anti-aircraft missile batteries and heroic repair crews who kept oil pumping onto tankers throughout the eight-year Tanker War.

single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_80.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Renowned for its red ochre beaches and rainbow-colored salt canyons, this tiny island features the ruins of an imposing 16th-century fortress built by Afonso de Albuquerque.
single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_80.explanation: Hormuz Island was the commercial pearl of the Indies until Safavid commander Imam Quli Khan expelled the Portuguese garrison در سال ۱۰۰۱ خورشیدی.

single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_10.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Originally named Gombroon and developed into Iran's primary container shipping port by Shah Abbas I, this coastal metropolis looks out over the Strait of Hormuz.
single_islands_and_ports_of_the_south_10.explanation: Home to the Shahid Rajaee container terminal, Bandar Abbas handles over half of Iran's maritime sea trade today.

single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: A towering playwright and director of Death of Yazdgerd and Bashu, the Little Stranger, this auteur is the grandmaster of historical allegorical theatre and film.
single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.explanation: Beyzai's research into pre-Islamic dramatic traditions culminated in his monumental book A Study of Iranian Theatre (سال ۱۳۴۳ خورشیدی).

single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Known as the 'poet of Iranian cinema' for his lyrical historical dialogues, this director created the immortal TV epic Hezar Dastan and the beloved tearjerker Mother (Madar).
single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.explanation: Hatami built the famous Ghazali Cinema Town in west Tehran to recreate 1930s Lalezar Street and the Tupkhaneh square for his cinematic works.

single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.clue_text: Directing Still Life (سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی) and A Simple Event, this pioneer of international cinematic minimalism emigrated to Germany and inspired directors like Chantal Akerman and Jim Jarmusch.
single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.explanation: Still Life won the Silver Bear at the سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی Berlin Film Festival, featuring an aging railway switchman told he is being retired after 33 years of routine.

single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.clue_text: Directing A Separation (سال ۱۳۹۰ خورشیدی) and The Salesman (سال ۱۳۹۵ خورشیدی), this contemporary master became the only Iranian director to win two Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film.
single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.explanation: A Separation also made history as the first foreign-language screenplay nominated for Best Original Screenplay at the Oscars.

single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.clue_text: This director won the Golden Leopard at Locarno for The Mirror (سال ۱۳۷۶ خورشیدی) and the Golden Bear at Berlin for Taxi (سال ۱۳۹۴ خورشیدی), despite being sentenced to a 20-year ban on filmmaking.
single_iranian_cinema_directors_and_aute.explanation: Panahi smuggled his film This Is Not a Film (سال ۱۳۹۰ خورشیدی) to the Cannes Film Festival hidden inside a USB flash drive baked inside a birthday cake.

single_music_radif_and_dastgah_200_encor.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Persian classical music is organized into this comprehensive canon of melodic motifs (Goushehs), arranged across seven primary modal systems (Dastgahs).
single_music_radif_and_dastgah_200_encor.explanation: Preserved by 19th-century court masters Mirza Abdollah and Aqa Hossein-Qoli, the Radif was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage در سال ۱۳۸۸ خورشیدی.

single_music_radif_and_dastgah_400_encor.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Revered as the undisputed 'Master' (Ostad) of Persian vocal music, this legendary baritone spent six decades mesmerizing millions with his breathtaking Tahrir vocal ornamentation.
single_music_radif_and_dastgah_400_encor.explanation: Shajarian's unaccompanied prayer 'Rabbana' was broadcast at sundown every Ramadan on Iranian radio for thirty years, becoming a sacred national soundscape.

single_music_radif_and_dastgah_600_encor.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Held vertically and played by directing air between the upper incisors and the tongue (Dandan technique), this end-blown reed flute was played with peerless virtuosity by Hasan Kasaei.
single_music_radif_and_dastgah_600_encor.explanation: The Ney opens Rumi's Masnavi with the immortal lament: 'Beshno az ney chon hekayat mikonad' (Listen to the reed as it tells its tale of separation).

single_music_radif_and_dastgah_800_encor.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Featuring a waist carved from solid mulberry wood covered in lamb fetus skin, this premier 25-fret long-necked lute is played with a brass plectrum encased in bee's wax.
single_music_radif_and_dastgah_800_encor.explanation: Renowned luthiers like Yahya of Isfahan in the early 20th century carved instruments whose resonance remains the gold standard in Iranian music.

single_music_radif_and_dastgah_1000_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Featuring 72 strings arranged in courses of four over 18 movable bridges, this trapezoidal wooden hammered dulcimer was brought to modern perfection by Ostad Faramarz Payvar.
single_music_radif_and_dastgah_1000_enco.explanation: The Santur is played using two delicate featherweight wooden hammers (mezrab), producing a crystalline, shimmering soundscape.

single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Grandson of Genghis Khan who sacked Baghdad in 1258, this Mongol ruler founded the Ilkhanate dynasty in Iran and established his capital at Tabriz and Maragheh.
single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.explanation: Hulagu embraced Persian culture and was persuaded by his astronomer vizier Nasir al-Din al-Tusi to construct the Maragheh Observatory in 1259.

single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Serving as Ilkhanid vizier to Ghazan Khan, this Jewish convert physician wrote Jami al-Tawarikh (Compendium of Chronicles), the world's first true universal history.
single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.explanation: Rashid al-Din built the Rab'-e Rashidi academy complex in Tabriz, employing hundreds of scholars, paper makers, and calligraphers to copy his historical manuscripts.

single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Founded in 1259 in Azerbaijan under Nasir al-Din al-Tusi, this astronomical observatory developed the 'Tusi-couple' geometrical model later utilized by Nicolaus Copernicus.
single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.explanation: Maragheh's 400,000-manuscript library and four-meter sextant produced the Zij-i Ilkhani planetary tables that circulated from China to Renaissance Italy.

single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Reigning from Samarkand, this astronomer-prince and grandson of Timur accurately calculated the sidereal year to within 25 seconds of modern measurements before being assassinated by his son.
single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.explanation: Ulugh Beg's star catalogue Zij-i Sultani (1437) mapped 1,018 stars, honored today by a crater on the Moon bearing his name.

single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Completed in 1430 for Timur's grandson Prince Baysunghur in Herat, this illustrated manuscript is universally revered as the supreme masterpiece of Persian miniature art.
single_ilkhanid_and_timurid_renaissance_.explanation: Inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register, its 21 surviving miniatures and calligraphy represent the zenith of the Timurid Herat School.

single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_200.clue_text: In اسفند/فروردین ۱۲۶۹, Nasir al-Din Shah granted this British major an exclusive 50-year worldwide monopoly over the production, sale, and export of all Iranian tobacco.
single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_200.explanation: Talbot paid £15,000 in personal bribes to Prime Minister Amin al-Soltan and promised £15,000 annually to the Shah plus a quarter of net profits.

single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_400.clue_text: Living in exile in Samarra (Iraq), this supreme Marja-e Taqlid issued the historic آذر ۱۲۷۰ fatwa that made smoking water-pipes equivalent to war against the Hidden Imam.
single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_400.explanation: The brief two-sentence fatwa spread by telegraph across Iran, uniting secular modernists, merchant guilds, and the clergy in the first successful mass civil disobedience movement.

single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_600.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Inside the royal palace harem, this favorite wife of Nasir al-Din Shah led his wives and concubines in smashing their crystal water-pipes (qalyan) in defiance of the sovereign.
single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_600.explanation: When the Shah asked who had forbidden smoking in his own palace, Anis al-Dowleh famously answered: 'The same one who made me lawful (halal) unto you.'

single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_800.clue_text: This fiery pan-Islamic activist wrote an urgent letter to Mirza Shirazi from Basra در سال ۱۲۷۰ خورشیدی detailing the betrayal of Iranian sovereignty before being expelled from Iran.
single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_800.explanation: Afghani had taken bast at Shah Abdol-Azim در سال ۱۲۶۹ خورشیدی before being dragged through snow by royal guards and dumped at the Ottoman frontier.

single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_100.clue_text: To cancel the Talbot concession in دی/بهمن ۱۲۷۰, the bankrupt Qajar state was forced to pay this enormous indemnity of £500,000, creating Iran's first foreign national debt.
single_the_tobacco_protest_forensics_100.explanation: The British-owned Imperial Bank of Persia lent the funds at 6% interest, secured against the customs revenues of the Persian Gulf ports.

double_provisional_regime_1979_400_encor.clue_text: A close medical aide to Khomeini in Neauphle-le-Château, this American-educated cancer researcher served as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister in the سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی provisional government.
double_provisional_regime_1979_400_encor.explanation: Yazdi and Bazargan met US National Security Advisor Zbigniew Brzezinski in Algiers on November 1, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, triggering the embassy takeover three days later.

double_provisional_regime_1979_800_encor.clue_text: Head of National Iranian Radio and Television and later Foreign Minister, this charismatic aide to Khomeini was executed by firing squad in Evin در سال ۱۳۶۱ خورشیدی for plotting to shell Jamaran.
double_provisional_regime_1979_800_encor.explanation: Ghotbzadeh was implicated alongside Grand Ayatollah Shariatmadari in an army plot to assassinate Khomeini and bomb the clerical leadership in Jamaran.

double_provisional_regime_1979_1200_enco.clue_text: Elected with 76% of the vote in دی/بهمن ۱۳۵۹, this Sorbonne economist wore simple civilian suits but was impeached by the Majles in خرداد ۱۳۵۹ and disguised himself to flee to Paris.
double_provisional_regime_1979_1200_enco.explanation: Banisadr allied with Massoud Rajavi's MEK against the Islamic Republic Party; after his impeachment, the MEK launched a campaign of assassinations that killed hundreds of leaders.

double_provisional_regime_1979_1600_enco.clue_text: Sprouting in mosques across every neighborhood in بهمن ۱۳۵۷, these armed local revolutionary councils seized weapons, policed streets, and arrested former royalist officials.
double_provisional_regime_1979_1600_enco.explanation: Headed by Ayatollah Mahdavi Kani, the Komitehs of the Islamic Revolution functioned as autonomous neighborhood fiefdoms until merged into the Law Enforcement Force (NAJA) در سال ۱۳۷۰ خورشیدی.

double_provisional_regime_1979_2000_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Serving as Secretary of the Revolutionary Council and later Majles Speaker and President, this pragmatist cleric from Rafsanjan was the central kingmaker of the new regime.
double_provisional_regime_1979_2000_enco.explanation: Rafsanjani survived an assassination attempt by the Forqan group in اردیبهشت ۱۳۵۷ and served as commander-in-chief of the war effort from سال ۱۳۶۷ خورشیدی.

double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_40.clue_text: به دنبال مهر ۱۳۵۲ Arab-Israeli War, the Shah led OPEC at the Tehran meeting to quadruple oil prices from $3 to nearly this benchmark price per barrel.
double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_40.explanation: Iran's petroleum revenues rocketed overnight from $5 billion در سال ۱۳۵۲ خورشیدی to over $20 billion در سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی, fueling the Shah's dream of creating the 'Great Civilization' (Tamaddon-e Bozorg).

double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_80.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Heading the Plan and Budget Organization, this Harvard-trained prince resigned after warning the Shah that pumping petrodollars into the economy would trigger runaway inflation.
double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_80.explanation: At the مرداد ۱۳۵۳ Ramsar conference, the Shah overruled economic planners and doubled the Fifth Plan budget, causing port congestion, cement shortages, and 30% inflation.

double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_12.clue_text: To combat soaring inflation در سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی, the Rastakhiz Party formed inspection squads that arrested over 20,000 shopkeepers and exiled 8,000 merchants under this controversial campaign.
double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_12.explanation: University students were sent with police to seal bazaar stalls and jail prominent merchants like Habib Elghanian, destroying the centuries-old alliance between monarchy and bazaar.

double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_16.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: During the petrodollar boom, this state-run automobile manufacturer produced hundreds of thousands of the Paykan, built under license from Britain's Hillman Hunter.
double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_16.explanation: Founded by brothers Ahmad and Mahmoud Khayyami در سال ۱۳۴۱ خورشیدی, Iran National made the Paykan ('Arrow') the ubiquitous national car of every Iranian family and taxi driver.

double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_20.clue_text: By سال ۱۳۵۵ خورشیدی, foreign cargo ships had to wait up to six months in the Persian Gulf to unload goods, costing the Iranian government over $1 billion annually in this shipping penalty fee.
double_economic_boom_and_petrodollars_20.explanation: Over two hundred cargo vessels queued outside Khorramshahr and Bandar Abbas while goods rotted in hulls, exposing the massive infrastructure bottlenecks of the boom.

double_revolutionary_tribunals_400_encor.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Appointed head of the Revolutionary Courts by Khomeini, this fiery cleric earned the moniker 'The Hanging Judge' for ordering hundreds of executions from the roof of Refah School.
double_revolutionary_tribunals_400_encor.explanation: Operating without defense attorneys or juries, Khalkhali executed over two hundred generals, ministers, and SAVAK officers in the first four months of the revolution.

double_revolutionary_tribunals_800_encor.clue_text: The iron-fisted martial law governor of Tehran who ordered troops to stand fast on ۲۲ بهمن ۱۳۵۷, this lieutenant general gave a defiant military salute before his execution.
double_revolutionary_tribunals_800_encor.explanation: Rahimi shouted 'Javid Shah!' (Long Live the King) and saluted before the firing squad on the snowy roof of Refah School at midnight on February 15, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی.

double_revolutionary_tribunals_1200_enco.clue_text: Before his execution in Evin in فروردین ۱۳۵۷, former Prime Minister Hoveyda asked for a cigarette and warned the court: 'A system built on this kind of justice...'
double_revolutionary_tribunals_1200_enco.explanation: Khalkhali shot Hoveyda in the neck during a recess to prevent Prime Minister Bazargan from obtaining a stay of execution from Khomeini in Qom.

double_revolutionary_tribunals_1600_enco.clue_text: Prominent Jewish philanthropist, plastics industrialist, and head of the Tehran Jewish community, his execution in اردیبهشت ۱۳۵۷ triggered the mass emigration of Iranian Jews.
double_revolutionary_tribunals_1600_enco.explanation: Elghanian built the famous Plasco building in Tehran; his execution on charges of 'Zionism and corruption' prompted US Senator Jacob Javits to introduce the first Congressional sanctions.

double_revolutionary_tribunals_2000_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Provisional Prime Minister Bazargan bitterly condemned the summary executions and secret trials in a famous television address, comparing the tribunals to this historical reign.
double_revolutionary_tribunals_2000_enco.explanation: Bazargan decried that 'the revolution has given birth to Robespierres who chop off heads without due process of law.'

single_the_oil_crisis_1951_1953_200_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Housing the world's largest oil refinery on the Shatt al-Arab, this island city in Khuzestan became the flashpoint of the nationalization confrontation with Britain.
single_the_oil_crisis_1951_1953_200_enco.explanation: In مهر ۱۳۳۰, Mosaddegh expelled the last remaining British engineers from Abadan, who sailed down the Shatt al-Arab aboard the cruiser HMS Mauritius.

single_the_oil_crisis_1951_1953_400_enco.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Known as the 'Soldier of Nationalization', this fiery orator and close lieutenant of Mosaddegh personally oversaw the seizure and unsealing of the Abadan refinery.
single_the_oil_crisis_1951_1953_400_enco.explanation: Makki rode atop oil tanks surrounded by thousands of cheering workers; his later defection from Mosaddegh was a major blow to the National Front.

single_the_oil_crisis_1951_1953_600_enco.clue_text: In تیر ۱۳۳۱ (30 Tir), millions of Iranians took to the streets in defiance of royal tanks to demand the reinstatement of Mosaddegh following his dismissal by this premier.
