single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_400.clue_text: در سال ۶۱۲ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, this Median warrior king formed an alliance with Nabopolassar of Babylon to storm and level Nineveh, annihilating the Assyrian Empire.
single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_400.explanation: Cyaxares reorganized Median armed forces into distinct archer, spearmen, and cavalry regiments, creating a professional army.

single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_600.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Modern city in the Zagros Mountains that sits atop the ancient Median capital Ecbatana (Hagmatana / Place of Gathering).
single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_600.explanation: Ecbatana served as the summer capital of Achaemenid, Parthian, and Sasanian monarchs seeking refuge from Mesopotamian heat.

single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_800.clue_text: The solar eclipse of May 28, ۵۸۵ پیش از میلاد, accurately predicted by Thales of Miletus, halted this decisive battle between Cyaxares and the Lydians.
single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_800.explanation: Both kings were terrified by day turning to night, immediately laying down weapons and sealing peace with royal dynastic marriages.

single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_100.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Excavated near Malayer in Hamadan, this Iron Age hill citadel site features the oldest surviving Zoroastrian fire temple tower in the world.
single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_100.explanation: Tepe Nush-i Jan contains an 8th-century BC central fire altar room with preserved mudbrick arched roofs carefully buried in shale before being abandoned.

single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_200.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Herodotus records that Astyages ordered his general Harpagus to murder the infant Cyrus because of a dream that his grandson's water would do this.
single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_200.explanation: Harpagus could not bring himself to murder the baby, handing him to a shepherd named Mithridates; Harpagus later defected to Cyrus in battle.

single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_400.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This ancient fortified mound in the Kangavar valley revealed 5,000-year-old ceramic jars with tartaric acid crystals, the world's oldest evidence of this beverage.
single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_400.explanation: Excavated by T. Cuyler Young Jr. at Godin Tepe, chemical analysis confirmed resinated grape wine and barley beer produced in 3500–۳۱۰۰ پیش از میلاد.

single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_600.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: According to Greek historians, the priestly sacerdotal caste among the Medes responsible for interpreting dreams, astrology, and sacrifices was known as this.
single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_600.explanation: The singular 'Magus' is the linguistic ancestor of the English words 'magic', 'magician', and the Biblical 'Three Wise Men'.

single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_800.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the Behistun Inscription, Darius the Great proudly proclaims that he quelled rebellions led by Fravartish, a Median rebel claiming to be of this king's lineage.
single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_800.explanation: Darius captured Fravartish at Rayy, impaling him on a stake at Ecbatana to extinguish Median dynastic revivals.

single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_100.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The Medes were renowned across the ancient Near East for their peerless breed of heavy cavalry horses, grazing in the lush pastures of this Kermanshah plain.
single_kings_of_the_medes_and_bounds_100.explanation: Nisean horses were the armored tanks of antiquity, capable of carrying cataphract knights clad in iron scale mail into battle.

single_sealed_with_a_diss_200_a.clue_text: Issued by Mozaffar al-Din Shah on ۱۴ مرداد ۱۲۸۵, this royal decree consented to the creation of a national consultative assembly (Majles).
single_sealed_with_a_diss_200_a.explanation: Signed by the dying Shah on his sickbed, it ordered the convening of an assembly of all estates to draft the fundamental law of the empire.

single_sealed_with_a_diss_400_a.clue_text: در سال ۱۱۸۶ خورشیدی, Napoleon Bonaparte signed this military alliance treaty with Fath-Ali Shah at a Prussian castle, promising to help Iran recover Georgia from Russia.
single_sealed_with_a_diss_400_a.explanation: Napoleon dispatched General Claude Mathieu de Gardane with 70 French military engineers to modernize the Iranian army before abandoning the alliance.

single_sealed_with_a_diss_600_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Carved into jade, carnelian, or ruby and dipped in black soot ink, this calligraphic signet seal was pressed onto royal letters by Iranian monarchs in place of a signature.
single_sealed_with_a_diss_600_a.explanation: The keeper of the royal seal (Mohrdar-e Saltanati) held immense power, stamping imperial firmans with the Shah's personal gem.

single_sealed_with_a_diss_800_a.clue_text: در سال ۱۲۵۲ خورشیدی, Nasir al-Din Shah became the first Iranian monarch to visit Europe, keeping an intimate diary describing his reception by this British Queen.
single_sealed_with_a_diss_800_a.explanation: Victoria invested Nasir al-Din Shah with the Order of the Garter at Windsor Castle, though royal courtiers were baffled by Persian dining etiquette.

single_sealed_with_a_diss_1000_a.clue_text: During the Tobacco Protests of سال ۱۲۷۰ خورشیدی, thousands of Iranian merchants and scholars took refuge from royal arrest inside this inviolable sanctuary space.
single_sealed_with_a_diss_1000_a.explanation: Traditional sites of Bast included holy shrines (Shah Abdol-Azim, Fatima Masumeh), royal stables, and the telegraph offices of the Indo-European line.

single_sealed_with_a_diss_200_b.clue_text: در سال ۱۲۲۷ خورشیدی, this British envoy and scholar of Cuneiform intervened repeatedly in Qajar court disputes, later publishing his memoirs on Persian politics.
single_sealed_with_a_diss_200_b.explanation: Rawlinson scaled the sheer limestone cliffs of Behistun with local boys to copy the trilingual cuneiform inscription.

single_sealed_with_a_diss_400_b.clue_text: This British diplomat authored the monumental two-volume سال ۱۲۷۰ خورشیدی travelogue Persia and the Persian Question before serving as British Foreign Secretary.
single_sealed_with_a_diss_400_b.explanation: Curzon regarded Iran as a vital buffer protecting British India, later authoring the ill-fated Anglo-Persian Agreement of سال ۱۲۹۸ خورشیدی.

single_sealed_with_a_diss_600_b.clue_text: On January 4, سال ۱۲۳۰ خورشیدی, royal executioner Ali Khan Hajeb al-Dowleh presented Nasir al-Din Shah with this tragic proof of Amir Kabir's death in Kashan.
single_sealed_with_a_diss_600_b.explanation: Nasir al-Din Shah wept bitterly upon hearing of his mentor's execution, regretting his rash order for the rest of his life.

single_sealed_with_a_diss_800_b.clue_text: در سال ۱۲۵۱ خورشیدی, Prime Minister Mirza Hosein Khan Moshir al-Dowleh arranged this sweeping concession granting Baron de Reuter control over all Iranian railways, mines, and forests.
single_sealed_with_a_diss_800_b.explanation: Lord Curzon called it 'the most complete surrender of the entire resources of a kingdom into foreign hands that has ever been dreamed of.'

single_sealed_with_a_diss_1000_b.clue_text: Under the سال ۱۲۰۶ خورشیدی Treaty of Turkmenchay, Russia imposed this extraterritorial legal immunity that prevented Iranian courts from prosecuting Russian subjects.
single_sealed_with_a_diss_1000_b.explanation: The capitulations were expanded to all European powers, later abolished by Reza Shah در سال ۱۳۰۷ خورشیدی, only to be revived for US military personnel در سال ۱۳۴۳ خورشیدی.

single_horsing_around_in_nisa_200_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: این شاخ‌های نوشیدنی باشکوه تراشیده‌شده از عاج فیل کشف‌شده در نسا با انتهای جانوران بالدار به این نام یونانی شناخته می‌شوند.
single_horsing_around_in_nisa_200_a.explanation: Over forty ivory rhytons were found in the royal treasure house of Nisa, blending Greek Hellenistic carving with Persian gryphon and lion motifs.

single_horsing_around_in_nisa_400_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Armored head-to-toe in overlapping iron or bronze scale mail and riding armored Nisean warhorses, these heavy Parthian shock cavalry were called this.
single_horsing_around_in_nisa_400_a.explanation: Cataphracts wielded a four-meter two-handed heavy lance (Kontos) capable of impaling two Roman legionaries at once.

single_horsing_around_in_nisa_600_a.clue_text: The founder of the Arsacid Parthian dynasty, a Parni chieftain who rebelled against the Seleucid satrap Andragoras around ۲۴۷ پیش از میلاد, was named this.
single_horsing_around_in_nisa_600_a.explanation: All subsequent thirty-one Parthian monarchs took the throne name 'Arsaces' (Ashk) on their official coinage to honor the dynastic founder.

single_horsing_around_in_nisa_800_a.clue_text: در سال ۱۴۱ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, this Parthian conqueror captured Seleucia-on-the-Tigris and Babylon, driving the Hellenistic Greeks out of the Iranian plateau.
single_horsing_around_in_nisa_800_a.explanation: Mithridates captured the Seleucid king Demetrius II Nicator alive, treating him honorably and giving him a Parthian princess in marriage.

single_horsing_around_in_nisa_1000_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The bronze statue of a tall Parthian nobleman wearing belted tunic and wide trousers with a dagger at his hip was unearthed at this Khuzestan site.
single_horsing_around_in_nisa_1000_a.explanation: Now in the National Museum of Iran, the 1.94-meter hollow-cast bronze statue is humanity's most striking portrait of an ancient Parthian grandee.

single_horsing_around_in_nisa_200_b.clue_text: در سال ۱۲۹ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, the last Seleucid army attempting to reconquer Iran was annihilated at Ecbatana and this Hellenistic emperor was killed in battle.
single_horsing_around_in_nisa_200_b.explanation: King Phraates II returned Antiochus's body to Syria in a silver coffin, permanently ending Greek rule east of the Euphrates River.

single_horsing_around_in_nisa_400_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The Parthian Empire was divided among seven great aristocratic families, of which this House, holding the hereditary right to crown the Shah, was the most powerful.
single_horsing_around_in_nisa_400_b.explanation: General Surena, victor of Carrhae, was the paramount chieftain of the House of Suren based in Sistan.

single_horsing_around_in_nisa_600_b.clue_text: در سال ۲۰ خورشیدی پیش از میلاد, Roman Emperor Augustus proudly celebrated a diplomatic triumph when Parthian King Phraates IV agreed to return these captured military relics.
single_horsing_around_in_nisa_600_b.explanation: Augustus commissioned the Prima Porta statue showing a bearded Parthian in trousers handing back the eagle standard to a Roman soldier.

single_horsing_around_in_nisa_800_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Excavated at Nisa, thousands of economic receipts were written with ink on fragments of broken pottery, known to archaeologists by this term.
single_horsing_around_in_nisa_800_b.explanation: Nisa's 2,700 ostraca record the wine harvests, vineyards, and royal taxes of the Arsacid kingdom in the Parthian language using the Aramaic alphabet.

single_horsing_around_in_nisa_1000_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The Parthian royal capital was shifted in summer to this ancient city in the Zagros mountains, where cool mountain breezes offered relief from the plains.
single_horsing_around_in_nisa_1000_b.explanation: Polybius described Ecbatana's royal palace under the Parthians, with its cedar and cypress roof beams completely clad in silver and gold plates.

single_shah_ping_for_antiques_200_a.clue_text: Commissioned by Nasir al-Din Shah در سال ۱۲۴۸ خورشیدی to locate unset gems, this 66-centimeter golden sphere is encrusted with over 51,000 diamonds, rubies, and emeralds.
single_shah_ping_for_antiques_200_a.explanation: The oceans are crafted from emeralds, Iran and Britain in diamonds, and southern Africa in rubies in the Central Bank vault.

single_shah_ping_for_antiques_400_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Weighing 182 carats and possessing an exceedingly rare pale pink tint, this table-cut diamond is the largest uncut pink diamond in the world.
single_shah_ping_for_antiques_400_a.explanation: Nader Shah brought the Daria-i-Noor from the Mughal treasury in Delhi در سال ۱۱۱۸ خورشیدی.

single_shah_ping_for_antiques_600_a.clue_text: Designed by French architect André Godard در سال ۱۳۱۶ خورشیدی, the entrance facade of the National Museum of Iran in Tehran is modeled on this Sasanian arch.
single_shah_ping_for_antiques_600_a.explanation: Godard used red Roman-sized fired bricks to evoke Sasanian imperial majesty for the Museum of Ancient Iran (Muzeh-ye Iran-e Bastan).

single_shah_ping_for_antiques_800_a.clue_text: Constructed for the سال ۱۳۰۵ خورشیدی coronation of Reza Shah, the Pahlavi Crown is topped by a plume of white egret feathers and encrusted with this many diamonds.
single_shah_ping_for_antiques_800_a.explanation: The crown features a massive 60-carat yellow diamond in the center of its sunburst, fabricated by master Caucasian jeweler Serajeddin.

single_shah_ping_for_antiques_1000_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Worn by Qajar monarchs from Fath-Ali Shah to Ahmad Shah, this tall velvet crown encrusted with 1,800 pearls and a giant spinel is known by this name.
single_shah_ping_for_antiques_1000_a.explanation: Taj-e Kiani was named after the mythical Kayanian kings of the Shahnameh, draped in red velvet and pearls.

single_shah_ping_for_antiques_200_b.clue_text: Discovered at Susa در سال ۱۲۸۱ خورشیدی, this life-size headless bronze statue of an Elamite queen weighing 1.8 tons is one of the prized treasures of the Louvre.
single_shah_ping_for_antiques_200_b.explanation: The base bears an inscription in Elamite cursing anyone who damages the statue with barrenness and divine wrath.

single_shah_ping_for_antiques_400_b.clue_text: Constructed در سال ۱۱۷۹ خورشیدی for Fath-Ali Shah's marriage to Tavous Khanum Taj al-Dowleh, this gold-leaf platform bed throne became famous as the Sun Throne.
single_shah_ping_for_antiques_400_b.explanation: Encrusted with 26,733 precious jewels, Takht-e Tavous was named after Tavous Khanum, whose title was Taj al-Dowleh.

single_shah_ping_for_antiques_600_b.clue_text: Under the سال ۱۲۷۴ خورشیدی archaeological concession granted by Nasir al-Din Shah, this European country held an exclusive monopoly over all excavations in Iran.
single_shah_ping_for_antiques_600_b.explanation: Director Jacques de Morgan shipped trainloads of gold and antiquities from Susa directly to the Louvre until Reza Shah abolished the monopoly در سال ۱۳۰۶ خورشیدی.

single_shah_ping_for_antiques_800_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Carved from dark green serpentine stone and featuring a golden rooster, this royal chest piece in the Treasury was worn by Qajar Shahs on ceremonial occasions.
single_shah_ping_for_antiques_800_b.explanation: The Bazuband originally held the Daria-i-Noor and Koh-i-Noor diamonds on opposite arms of Nader Shah.

single_shah_ping_for_antiques_1000_b.clue_text: در سال ۱۳۱۶ خورشیدی, Reza Shah placed the entire Imperial Crown Jewels in the vault of this newly created state financial institution as backing for the national currency.
single_shah_ping_for_antiques_1000_b.explanation: By law, the Crown Jewels cannot be sold and remain the physical collateral for the Iranian Rial in the Central Bank vault on Ferdowsi Avenue.

single_damavand_ing_respect_200_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Rising 5,609 meters above sea level in the Alborz range, this dormant stratovolcano is the highest peak in Iran and the highest volcano in Asia.
single_damavand_ing_respect_200_a.explanation: Damavand features year-round summit glaciers, active sulfur fumaroles near its crater, and is celebrated in Bahar's ode 'O white demon with chained feet'.

single_damavand_ing_respect_400_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: According to Persian legend, this heroic archer climbed Mount Damavand to loose an arrow that flew for three days, establishing the boundary between Iran and Turan.
single_damavand_ing_respect_400_a.explanation: Siavash Kasra'i's سال ۱۳۳۸ خورشیدی modern epic poem Arash-e Kamangir made the archer an enduring symbol of self-sacrificing patriotic martyrdom.

single_damavand_ing_respect_600_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the Shahnameh, the tyrant Zahhak, with flesh-eating serpents sprouting from his shoulders, was captured by Fereydun and chained in a cave beneath this peak.
single_damavand_ing_respect_600_a.explanation: Legend holds that sulfur fumes and earthquakes emanating from Damavand are the fiery breathing and thrashing of the chained tyrant Zahhak.

single_damavand_ing_respect_800_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Flowing through a dramatic gorge carved into the Alborz along the foot of Damavand, this river empties into the Caspian Sea near Babolsar.
single_damavand_ing_respect_800_a.explanation: The Haraz Road (Road 77) carved along the canyon walls is one of the most treacherous and spectacular mountain highways in the world.

single_damavand_ing_respect_1000_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Located on the southern slopes of Damavand, this alpine national park is famous for wild scarlet poppy fields blooming each spring against snowy peaks.
single_damavand_ing_respect_1000_a.explanation: Lar Dam reservoirs provide drinking water to Tehran, surrounded by meadows hosting rare endemic brown trout (Qezel-ala).

single_damavand_ing_respect_200_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Standing 4,848 meters high in Mazandaran, this second-highest peak in Iran is renowned among mountaineers for its vertical 800-meter granite rock wall.
single_damavand_ing_respect_200_b.explanation: Alam-Kuh's northern granite face is compared by alpinists to the Grandes Jorasses and the north wall of the Matterhorn in the Alps.

single_damavand_ing_respect_400_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This critically endangered big cat, with barely 40 surviving individuals clinging to existence in the central Iranian deserts, is this animal.
single_damavand_ing_respect_400_b.explanation: Iran's national football team wore the Asiatic cheetah on their World Cup jerseys to raise international awareness for its conservation.

single_damavand_ing_respect_600_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Extending along the northern slopes of the Alborz and the Caspian Sea, these 50-million-year-old ancient temperate rainforests are a UNESCO World Heritage site.
single_damavand_ing_respect_600_b.explanation: Surviving the Ice Ages as a botanical refugium, the Hyrcanian forests house relict Tertiary trees like the Persian ironwood (Parrotia persica).

single_damavand_ing_respect_800_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Rising 4,811 meters in Ardabil province, this dormant volcanic peak features a natural freshwater crater lake at its summit that freezes into ice for nine months a year.
single_damavand_ing_respect_800_b.explanation: Local Azeri folklore holds that the prophet Zoroaster lived and meditated on the slopes of Sabalan.

single_damavand_ing_respect_1000_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The longest river entirely within the borders of Iran, rising in the Zagros and flowing past Ahvaz into the Shatt al-Arab, is this river.
single_damavand_ing_respect_1000_b.explanation: Spanning 950 kilometers, the Karun is the only navigable river in Iran, where British steamships operated trade routes in the late 19th century.

single_poets_in_exile_200_a.clue_text: A master of imagist modern verse, this poet fled to Los Angeles after سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, famously longing for Tehran in poems like Collyrium of the Sun.
single_poets_in_exile_200_a.explanation: Naderpour lived in California until his death در سال ۱۳۷۹ خورشیدی, his gravestone inscribed with his famous poem 'My sorrow is an ancient forest.'

single_poets_in_exile_400_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Co-author of The Cow and leading dramatist, this medical doctor fled into French exile where he drank himself to death, buried in Père Lachaise near Sadegh Hedayat.
single_poets_in_exile_400_a.explanation: Writing under the pseudonym Gowhar Morad, Sa'edi died of gastrointestinal bleeding in Paris در سال ۱۳۶۳ خورشیدی.

single_poets_in_exile_600_a.clue_text: Living in East Berlin for four decades after the سال ۱۳۳۲ خورشیدی coup, this author of Her Eyes taught Persian literature at Humboldt University.
single_poets_in_exile_600_a.explanation: Alavi returned briefly to Iran after the سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی revolution, but returned to Berlin where he died در سال ۱۳۷۶ خورشیدی.

single_poets_in_exile_800_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This brilliant satirist and diplomat penned the comic masterpiece My Uncle Napoleon (Da'i Jan Napoleon) in Geneva and Paris exile.
single_poets_in_exile_800_a.explanation: My Uncle Napoleon satirized the widespread Iranian paranoia of British conspiracy, adapted into a record-shattering سال ۱۳۵۵ خورشیدی television series by Nasser Taghvai.

single_poets_in_exile_1000_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Author of the feminist novella Women Without Men (Zanan bedun-e Mardan), this woman was repeatedly jailed in the 1980s before settling in the US.
single_poets_in_exile_1000_a.explanation: Her book was adapted into a Venice Silver Lion-winning film by Shirin Neshat در سال ۱۳۸۸ خورشیدی.

single_poets_in_exile_200_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: A leading critic and poet who wrote The Crowned Cannibals on SAVAK torture, he was exiled to Canada where he taught at the University of Toronto.
single_poets_in_exile_200_b.explanation: Baraheni was president of the Writers' Association of Iran and wrote the acclaimed post-revolutionary novel The Secrets of My Homeland.

single_poets_in_exile_400_b.clue_text: A philosopher who coined the term 'Cultural Schizophrenia' to describe the dilemma of modern Muslims caught between Western modernity and Asian tradition, he died in Paris در سال ۱۳۹۷ خورشیدی.
single_poets_in_exile_400_b.explanation: Shayegan was awarded the prestigious French Academy Francophonie medal for his books written in French examining Indian and Persian thought.

single_poets_in_exile_600_b.clue_text: Renowned intellectual and filmmaker who produced The Brick and the Mirror, he emigrated to England in the 1970s, residing at Wykehurst Park until his death at age 101 در سال ۱۴۰۲ خورشیدی.
single_poets_in_exile_600_b.explanation: Golestan was the romantic and intellectual partner of poet Forough Farrokhzad, managing Golestan Film Studio in Tehran.

single_poets_in_exile_800_b.clue_text: Living in Geneva for over seventy years until his death at 102 در سال ۱۳۷۶ خورشیدی, this pioneer of Persian short stories donated his massive library to the University of Tehran.
single_poets_in_exile_800_b.explanation: Jamalzadeh represented Iran at the International Labour Organization (ILO) in Geneva from سال ۱۳۱۰ خورشیدی to سال ۱۳۳۵ خورشیدی.

single_poets_in_exile_1000_b.clue_text: Author of Tangsir and The Patient Stone, this realist fiction master emigrated to the United States in the late 1970s, dying blind in Berkeley, California در سال ۱۳۷۷ خورشیدی.
single_poets_in_exile_1000_b.explanation: Chubak requested that all his unpublished manuscripts and private diaries be cremated with his body upon his death.

single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Baked on a sloping bed of burning river pebbles in giant dome ovens, this whole wheat sourdough flatbread is considered the king of traditional Iranian breads.
single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.explanation: Sangak ('little pebbles') was historically invented for Persian armies on the march, where soldiers carried river stones to build portable ovens.

single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Brought to Tehran in the late 19th century by Hazara and Khorasani immigrants, this thick oval crusty bread glazed with baking soda wash is named after this ethnic group.
single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.explanation: Barbari refers to the Hazara community of eastern Khorasan who originally operated the bakeries in southern Tehran.

single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.clue_text: In آذر ۱۳۲۱, grain hoarding and Allied requisitioning caused starving crowds to storm the Majles and riot over bread in this capital city.
single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.explanation: Protesters looted Prime Minister Qavam's private residence after discovering sawdust and pebbles baked into municipal loaves.

single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.clue_text: Introduced در سال ۱۳۵۹ خورشیدی during the Iran-Iraq War, this system of colored ration coupons for meat, sugar, rice, and cooking oil was known by this French loanword.
single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.explanation: Kupon-e bazi (coupon trading) created a parallel black market economy that sustained working-class families throughout the eight-year war.

single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: To keep food prices artificially low in the 1970s, the Pahlavi state created this giant consumer cooperative agency with subsidized supermarkets across Iran.
single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.explanation: Koorosh department stores were targeted for nationalization در سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی and renamed Forushgah-e Qods.

single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.clue_text: Under the سال ۱۳۰۴ خورشیدی railway law, Minister Davar imposed state monopolies and excise taxes on sugar and tea to finance this national infrastructure project.
single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.explanation: The sugar and tea monopoly raised 120 million tomans over twelve years, allowing the 1,394-km railway to be built without a single pound of foreign debt.

single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.clue_text: در سال ۱۲۸۴ خورشیدی, the public bastinado of sugar merchants by the governor of Tehran over price inflation sparked this revolution.
single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.explanation: Governor Ala al-Dowleh ordered prominent merchant Seyyed Hashem Ghandi beaten on his bare soles, causing bazaar shops to close and clerics to march to Rey.

single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.clue_text: در سال ۱۳۸۹ خورشیدی, President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad abolished direct price subsidies on bread, gasoline, and electricity, replacing them with this cash payment program.
single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.explanation: Every Iranian citizen received approximately 45,500 tomans (about $45 در سال ۱۳۸۹ خورشیدی) per month directly deposited into bank accounts.

single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This paper-thin unfermented flatbread, rolled out with wooden dowels and baked in seconds on a hot concave steel disc (Saj), is baked in villages across Iran.
single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.explanation: Lavash was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage در سال ۱۳۹۵ خورشیدی.

single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.clue_text: During the سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی Anti-Profiteering Campaign, thousands of guild butchers were fined or jailed for refusing to sell red meat below this benchmark price.
single_the_bread_and_butter_of_politics_.explanation: Enforced by university students carrying Rastakhiz Party batons, price ceilings drove red meat and butter out of butcher shops into underground black markets.

single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_200_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Engineered through solid mountain rock by Austrian and local workers in the 1930s, this winding scenic highway links Karaj to the Caspian port of Chaloos.
single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_200_a.explanation: The 1,884-meter Kandovan Tunnel, hand-chiseled through the Alborz mountain crest در سال ۱۳۱۷ خورشیدی, cut travel time from Tehran to the Caspian from days to hours.

single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_400_a.clue_text: در سال ۱۳۴۱ خورشیدی, brothers Ahmad and Mahmoud Khayyami founded this premier industrial giant to assemble the Paykan under license from Britain's Rootes Group.
single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_400_a.explanation: Between سال ۱۳۴۶ خورشیدی and سال ۱۳۸۴ خورشیدی, over two million Paykans were manufactured, becoming the ubiquitous chariot of Iranian middle-class life.

single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_600_a.clue_text: در سال ۱۲۷۹ خورشیدی, this monarch purchased Iran's first two automobiles—twin open-top French Gardner-Serpollet steam carriages—during his tour of Belgium and Paris.
single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_600_a.explanation: One car broke down en route through the Caucasus mountains; the surviving carriage was driven in Tehran by French chauffeur Monsieur Varelet.

single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_800_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The British Rootes Group vehicle that served as the chassis and mechanical design base for the Iranian Paykan was known by this model name in the UK.
single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_800_a.explanation: The 1725cc four-cylinder engine and sturdy leaf-spring rear suspension were uniquely suited to rough Iranian provincial roads.

single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_1000_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Located in northern Tehran, this former imperial estate houses the Royal Automobile Museum exhibiting bulletproof Rolls-Royces, Mercedes 600s, and Ferraris.
single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_1000_a.explanation: The museum features an extraordinary bespoke electric Panther De Ville, gifts from international monarchs, and the Shah's personal Porsche 911.

single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_200_b.clue_text: During his سال ۱۲۷۹ خورشیدی state visit to Belgium, Mozaffar al-Din Shah survived an assassination attempt in Brussels by an anarchist armed with this weapon.
single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_200_b.explanation: Anarchist François Salson aimed the gun at the Shah's chest, but Grand Vizier Atabak seized the assailant's wrist and wrestled him to the pavement.

single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_400_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The iconic orange color and roof light of taxis across Tehran and provincial cities became synonymous with this ubiquitous vehicle.
single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_400_b.explanation: The distinctive roar of the Paykan engine and clinking gearbox formed the soundtrack of Tehran rush-hour traffic for nearly four decades.

single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_600_b.clue_text: The massive four-lane highway linking Tehran to Karaj opened در سال ۱۳۴۵ خورشیدی as Iran's first modern limited-access toll freeway, known as this.
single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_600_b.explanation: It handled commuter traffic between the capital and the burgeoning industrial parks and auto plants established in Karaj and Alborz.

single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_800_b.clue_text: This French automobile, built under license by SAIPA starting در سال ۱۳۴۷ خورشیدی with a canvas rollback roof and swinging suspension, was affectionately called the Jian.
single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_800_b.explanation: Jian ('ferocious/brave' in Persian) was beloved for its ability to navigate unpaved village ruts and riverbeds without getting stuck.

single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_1000_b.clue_text: در سال ۱۳۵۰ خورشیدی, this American automaker established 'General Motors Iran' in Tehran, assembling Cadillac Sevilles, Buick Skylarks, and Chevrolet Novas.
single_a_rolls_royce_for_reza_1000_b.explanation: The Cadillac Seville built in Tehran was the only Cadillac model ever assembled outside of the United States prior to the 21st century.

single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_200_.clue_text: Revered as the Robin Hood of the Caspian forests, this bearded cleric established the anti-imperialist Jangal (Forest) guerrilla movement در سال ۱۲۹۴ خورشیدی.
single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_200_.explanation: Mirza Kuchik Khan proclaimed the Soviet Republic of Gilan in Rasht in خرداد ۱۲۹۹ with Red Army support.

single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_400_.clue_text: In خرداد ۱۲۹۹, Bolshevik naval vessels landed at this Caspian port, driving out British forces and establishing the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic.
single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_400_.explanation: Admiral Fyodor Raskolnikov led the Caspian Flotilla that shelled British forces withdrawing down the Manjil road to Qazvin.

single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_600_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Harvested from the beluga sturgeon native to the southern Caspian Sea, this black roe was world-renowned as Iran's most luxurious culinary export.
single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_600_.explanation: Under the Qajars, Russian industrialist Stepan Lianozov held the exclusive concession over Caspian fisheries (Shilat).

single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_800_.clue_text: Introduced by Kashef al-Saltaneh who smuggled seedlings out of British India in his walking stick in ۱۸۹۹, this crop blankets the hills of Lahijan.
single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_800_.explanation: Mohammad Mirza Kashef al-Saltaneh is commemorated as the 'Father of Iranian Tea' at the National Tea Museum in Lahijan.

single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_1000.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This fairytale terraced village in Gilan features mud-straw houses built into the mountainside where the roof of one house serves as the courtyard of the house above.
single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_1000.explanation: Masuleh's unique interconnected architecture forbids all motor vehicles, creating an idyllic car-free pedestrian village.

single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_200_.clue_text: In آذر ۱۲۹۹, Mirza Kuchik Khan died of hypothermia in a blizzard in these mountains while fleeing Reza Khan's army.
single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_200_.explanation: A local landowner severed his frozen head and delivered it to Reza Khan in Tehran, where it was displayed on a pole before burial.

single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_400_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Built during the Sasanian era to protect the Caspian frontier from White Hun nomads, this 195-kilometer brick fortification is the Great Wall of this city.
single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_400_.explanation: Known as the 'Red Snake' for its red fired bricks, it was the longest continuous brick wall built in antiquity, exceeding Hadrian's Wall.

single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_600_.clue_text: On June 21, سال ۱۳۶۹ خورشیدی, this catastrophic magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck Gilan and Zanjan, inspiring Abbas Kiarostami's acclaimed film Life, and Nothing More...
single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_600_.explanation: The disaster killed over 40,000 people and destroyed the towns of Rudbar, Manjil, and Lowshan along the Sefid-Rud gorge.

single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_800_.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Originating in Gilan, this sour herb and split pea stew cooked with garlic, verjuice (ab-ghooreh), and braised chicken or duck is known as this.
single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_800_.explanation: Torshi Tareh showcases the unique sour Caspian palate derived from abundant fresh herbs, wild garlic, and citrus verjuice.

single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_1000.clue_text: The massive concrete gravity dam built در سال ۱۳۴۱ خورشیدی across the Sefid-Rud at Manjil to irrigate the rice paddies of the Gilan delta was named this.
single_tales_from_the_caspian_shore_1000.explanation: Originally named Shahbanu Farah Dam, its 106-meter-high concrete buttresses withstood the violent سال ۱۳۶۹ خورشیدی earthquake with minor structural cracks.

single_persian_flights_of_fancy_200_a.clue_text: Designed در سال ۱۳۴۰ خورشیدی by 22-year-old art student Edward Zohrabian, the iconic logo of Iran Air depicts this mythical Persian griffin-bird found at Persepolis.
single_persian_flights_of_fancy_200_a.explanation: Homa (the mythical bird of good fortune that bestows sovereignty upon whose head it casts a shadow) was acclaimed by IATA as one of the world's most beautiful airline logos.

single_persian_flights_of_fancy_400_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the mid-1970s, Iran Air was the first international airline to operate this specialized ultra-long-range Boeing aircraft nonstop between Tehran and New York.
single_persian_flights_of_fancy_400_a.explanation: The Boeing 747SP ('Special Performance') featured a shortened fuselage and taller tail fin, allowing Iran Air to complete the 6,336-mile trans-Atlantic flight in 11 hours.

single_persian_flights_of_fancy_600_a.clue_text: Designed by architect Iraj Moshiri, this main international airport of Tehran served as Iran's primary aviation gateway from سال ۱۳۳۷ خورشیدی until commercial long-haul flights moved south.
single_persian_flights_of_fancy_600_a.explanation: Mehrabad's modernist concrete passenger terminal was celebrated for its dramatic sweeping roofline and views of snowy Mount Damavand.

single_persian_flights_of_fancy_800_a.clue_text: Commander of the Imperial Iranian Air Force's Golden Crown aerobatic team and head of physical education, this charismatic general was executed on the Refah School roof در سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی.
single_persian_flights_of_fancy_800_a.explanation: Known as the 'Blue-Eyed General', Jahanbani reportedly refused a blindfold before the firing squad, declaring: 'I am proud of my service to Iranian aviation.'

single_persian_flights_of_fancy_1000_a.clue_text: On ۱۲ بهمن ۱۳۵۷, Ayatollah Khomeini returned to Tehran from sixteen years of exile aboard a chartered Boeing 747 operated by this national airline.
single_persian_flights_of_fancy_1000_a.explanation: Aboard the flight, ABC News correspondent Peter Jennings asked Khomeini what he felt returning to Iran after so long, to which he famously answered: 'Nothing' (Hichi).

single_persian_flights_of_fancy_200_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Purchased by the Shah in the mid-1970s with cutting-edge AWG-9 radars and Phoenix missiles, Iran became the only foreign country ever to operate this legendary swing-wing fighter jet.
single_persian_flights_of_fancy_200_b.explanation: Iran's 79 Tomcats scored over 160 air-to-air kills against Iraqi MiGs and Mirages, creating top aces like Major Jalil Zandi with 11 confirmed kills.

single_persian_flights_of_fancy_400_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Built in the late 1960s with luxurious bespoke private suites and gold-plated fixtures, the Shah's private VIP Boeing 707 was christened with this imperial name.
single_persian_flights_of_fancy_400_b.explanation: The Shah personally piloted the Shahin when he and Empress Farah flew out of Mehrabad into final exile on January 16, سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی.

single_persian_flights_of_fancy_600_b.clue_text: On April 4, سال ۱۳۵۹ خورشیدی, eight Iranian F-4 Phantoms flew 1,800 miles with multiple mid-air refuelings to destroy 48 Iraqi aircraft at this remote airbase complex near the Jordanian border.
single_persian_flights_of_fancy_600_b.explanation: Considered one of the most audacious deep-penetration airstrikes in military aviation history, Iranian jets flew below radar along the Iraqi-Turkish-Syrian borders.

single_persian_flights_of_fancy_800_b.clue_text: Opened در سال ۱۳۸۳ خورشیدی thirty kilometers southwest of Tehran, this modern international airport replaced Mehrabad for all international commercial flights.
single_persian_flights_of_fancy_800_b.explanation: On its scheduled opening day in اردیبهشت ۱۳۸۳, the Revolutionary Guards forced the airport to close using armored vehicles to protest a Turkish operator contract.

single_persian_flights_of_fancy_1000_b.clue_text: In بهمن ۱۳۵۷, the mutiny of these technical air force apprentices (Homafaran) at Doshan Tappeh airbase triggered the final street insurrection that toppled the monarchy.
single_persian_flights_of_fancy_1000_b.explanation: Trained in the US on modern jet engines, the Homafaran distributed thousands of assault rifles from base armories to civilian guerrillas, sealing the regime's fate.

single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_200_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the First Labor of the Haft Khan, Rostam was asleep when his faithful warhorse Rakhsh fought and trampled this ferocious predator to death.
single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_200_a.explanation: Rostam chided Rakhsh for risking his life alone, warning him: 'If you had been slain, who would have carried my heavy armor into Mazandaran?'

single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_400_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the Second Labor, dying of dehydration in the scorching desert sands, Rostam prayed to God and was miraculously guided to a water spring by this animal.
single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_400_a.explanation: Rostam praised the Creator for sending the divine ram, quenching his and Rakhsh's thirst before facing the fire-breathing dragon.

single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_600_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the Fourth Labor, Rostam sat beside an enchanted stream and sang of his sorrows until this enchantress approached disguised as a beautiful damsel.
single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_600_a.explanation: When Rostam handed her a goblet of wine and uttered the name of God, the illusion broke and her true black demonic form was revealed, whereupon Rostam lassooed and cleaved her in two.

single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_800_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the Fifth Labor, Rostam captured this local border chieftain, promising to make him King of Mazandaran if he guided him through the dark enchantments.
single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_800_a.explanation: Bound with a leather lariat, Oulad faithfully guided Rostam past the bottomless pits and scorching winds to the cavern of the White Demon.

single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_1000_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In the Sixth Labor, Rostam decapitated this demonic champion outside his fortress, throwing his army into panic.
single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_1000_a.explanation: Rostam charged Arzhang's camp shouting like thunder, tore off his head with his bare hands, and hurled it into the ranks of the Mazandaran demons.

single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_200_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The entire Haft Khan expedition was launched to rescue this foolish, arrogant Iranian monarch who had marched into Mazandaran and been captured and blinded by demons.
single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_200_b.explanation: Kavus was seduced by a demon minstrel singing of the endless spring of Mazandaran, leading his army into blindness and captivity.

single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_400_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: To restore the sight of the blinded King Kay Kavus and the Iranian paladins, Rostam poured three drops of this into their eyes.
single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_400_b.explanation: The physician priests declared that only the hot liver blood of the White Demon could burn away the demonic cataract blinding their pupils.

single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_600_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Rostam's massive signature weapon, forged by Kaveh the Blacksmith with the likeness of an ox's head on its iron pommel, was known as this.
single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_600_b.explanation: Inherited from his grandfather Sam and King Fereydun, the ox-headed mace crushed the skulls of demons and armored knights with a single blow.

single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_800_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Rostam's mythical stallion, intelligent enough to wake his master, kill lions, and understand human speech, was named this.
single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_800_b.explanation: Rakhsh was described as having a coat like rose petals scattered on saffron, chosen by Rostam when no other stallion could support his weight.

single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_1000_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The invulnerable, waterproof battle tunic worn by Rostam into battle, fashioned from the skin of a mythical sea beast or leopard, was called this.
single_the_seven_labors_of_rostam_1000_b.explanation: The coat was impervious to fire, water, and arrows, protecting Rostam through centuries of warfare.

single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_200_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Regarded as the 'Bride of Islamic Calligraphic Scripts', this flowing, cursive Persian script was invented in the 14th century by Mir Ali Tabrizi.
single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_200_a.explanation: Nastaliq combines Naskh and Ta'liq, inspired according to legend by the graceful curves of flying geese.

single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_400_a.clue_text: Serving at the court of Shah Abbas I in Isfahan, this supreme calligrapher was murdered in ۱۶۱۵ by jealous courtiers, his style remaining the benchmark of Nastaliq.
single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_400_a.explanation: Mir Emad's individual calligraphic folios (Qet'eh) were traded across India, the Ottoman Empire, and Europe for their weight in gold.

single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_600_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Invented in the 17th century for fast administrative court correspondence, this ornate broken script was perfected by Darvish Abdol-Majid Taleqani.
single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_600_a.explanation: Shekasteh linked letters that were traditionally unjoined, creating dynamic visual rhythms resembling swaying branches.

single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_800_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Persian scribes crafted luxury carrying cases for their reed pens and inkwells using lacquered papier-mâché painted with nightingales and roses, known by this name.
single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_800_a.explanation: Qalamdans were sliding wooden or papier-mâché sleeves tucked into a scribe's belt sash, painted by master Qajar miniaturists.

single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_1000_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The finest reed pens (Qalam-e Ney) used by Iranian calligraphers are harvested from the dense river reed-beds of this southern Khuzestan city.
single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_1000_a.explanation: Dezful reeds are seasoned for months until they turn glossy dark brown and ring like porcelain when struck.

single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_200_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Traditional Persian black ink (Morakkab) was brewed by boiling fine soot with gum arabic and the crushed gallnuts of this tree.
single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_200_b.explanation: The reaction between oak gall tannic acid and iron sulfate created indelible black ink that remained glossy for centuries.

single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_400_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The practice sheets where calligraphers repeatedly inscribed intersecting diagonal words until the paper turned into an abstract dense black carpet are called this.
single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_400_b.explanation: Originally practical exercises to warm up fingers, Qajar masters like Mirza Gholam-Reza Esfahani transformed Siah-Mashq into high abstract art.

single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_600_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The fine floral illumination in 24-karat liquid gold leaf and lapis lazuli framing calligraphic panels and Quranic headers is known by this Arabic-derived term.
single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_600_b.explanation: Tazhib derives from Zahab (gold in Arabic), requiring artists to grind real gold leaves into powder and apply it with single-hair brushes.

single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_800_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Under the Safavids and Qajars, official imperial decrees bore this monumental calligraphic monogram containing the names and titles of the Shah at the top.
single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_800_b.explanation: Tughrawis were elite court scribes specializing in drawing the interlacing vertical strokes of the imperial signature.

single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_1000_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: To cut the sharp angled nib of a reed pen, calligraphers placed the reed on this small carved piece of bone, tortoiseshell, or ivory called a Qalam-tarash.
single_calligraphy_and_inkwells_1000_b.explanation: A sharp click (Qat) as the pen knife severed the reed against the bone plate signaled a perfect nib angle for Nastaliq.

single_the_shahs_secret_illness_200_a.clue_text: In اردیبهشت ۱۳۵۳, French hematologists Georges Flandrin and Jean Bernard secretly diagnosed the Shah with this rare cancer of the lymphatic system.
single_the_shahs_secret_illness_200_a.explanation: The Shah demanded complete secrecy; even Empress Farah Diba was kept in the dark about the fatal diagnosis until autumn سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی.

single_the_shahs_secret_illness_400_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: To conceal his treatments from the CIA and Iranian public, French doctors flew into Tehran on commercial flights carrying drugs labeled under this cover name.
single_the_shahs_secret_illness_400_a.explanation: The Shah feared showing physical weakness would encourage Khomeini and cause Washington to seek an alternative leader.

single_the_shahs_secret_illness_600_a.clue_text: In مهر ۱۳۵۷, President Jimmy Carter reluctantly allowed the exiled Shah into the United States for emergency medical treatment at this hospital.
single_the_shahs_secret_illness_600_a.explanation: Admitted under the alias 'David D. Newsom', the Shah's presence in New York provoked the storming of the US Embassy in Tehran two weeks later.

single_the_shahs_secret_illness_800_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: After being expelled from the United States and Panama, the dying Shah was granted unconditional royal asylum in Cairo by this Egyptian President.
single_the_shahs_secret_illness_800_a.explanation: Sadat declared: 'The Shah helped Egypt when we were alone; I will not abandon him when the world turns its back.'

single_the_shahs_secret_illness_1000_a.clue_text: Famed Houston heart surgeon who flew to Cairo in اسفند/فروردین ۱۳۵۹ to perform a splenectomy on the Shah was named this.
single_the_shahs_secret_illness_1000_a.explanation: DeBakey removed the Shah's massive 3.5-kilogram leukemic spleen at Maadi Military Hospital in Cairo.

single_the_shahs_secret_illness_200_b.clue_text: On July 27, سال ۱۳۵۹ خورشیدی, Mohammad Reza Shah died at age 60 in Cairo, entombed inside this historic royal mosque alongside Egypt's Khedive Ismail.
single_the_shahs_secret_illness_200_b.explanation: His father Reza Shah had also been interred temporarily in Al-Rifa'i Mosque در سال ۱۳۲۳ خورشیدی before being brought to Rey.

single_the_shahs_secret_illness_400_b.clue_text: The Shah's longtime Court Minister and confidant, he was diagnosed with the exact same lymphoma cancer و درگذشت در New York in فروردین ۱۳۵۷.
single_the_shahs_secret_illness_400_b.explanation: Alam's death deprived the Shah of his closest political sounding board just as the revolutionary crisis escalated.

single_the_shahs_secret_illness_600_b.clue_text: During his island exile off Panama in early سال ۱۳۵۹ خورشیدی, the Shah was pressured by this Panamanian military strongman who flirted with extraditing him.
single_the_shahs_secret_illness_600_b.explanation: The Shah fled Contadora Island on a chartered chartered DC-8 hours before Panamanian authorities could serve extradition papers from Tehran.

single_the_shahs_secret_illness_800_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The Shah's intense secret chemotherapy regimen caused severe depression, apathy, and cognitive exhaustion, which historians cite for his hesitation during this year.
single_the_shahs_secret_illness_800_b.explanation: Heavy doses of chlorambucil and prednisone contributed to the Shah's paralysis of will, oscillating between martial crackdowns and weeping apologies.

single_the_shahs_secret_illness_1000_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: In his final dying interview in Cairo with British journalist David Frost, the Shah declared: 'I made one big mistake...'
single_the_shahs_secret_illness_1000_b.explanation: His final French memoir was titled Réponse à l'histoire (Answer to History), published posthumously در سال ۱۳۵۹ خورشیدی.

double_ayat_all_that_400_a.clue_text: In his سال ۱۳۴۹ خورشیدی Najaf lectures, Ayatollah Khomeini articulated this radical political doctrine asserting that the supreme Islamic jurist must rule the state directly.
double_ayat_all_that_400_a.explanation: Published as Islamic Government: Governance of the Jurist, it broke with centuries of quietist Shi'i theology awaiting the return of the Hidden Imam.

double_ayat_all_that_800_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The traditional Shi'i legal school that championed rational deduction (Ijtihad) over literal scriptural traditions in the 18th century is known as this.
double_ayat_all_that_800_a.explanation: Led by Vahid Behbahani in Karbala, the Usuli victory established the absolute authority of living Mujtahids over the faithful.

double_ayat_all_that_1200_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The Shi'i religious tax of one-fifth levied on annual surplus wealth, channeled directly to Grand Ayatollahs to fund seminaries and stipends, is this.
double_ayat_all_that_1200_a.explanation: Khums is divided into Sahm-e Imam (Share of the Imam) and Sahm-e Sadat (Share of the Prophet's descendants), giving the Hawza financial independence from the state.

double_ayat_all_that_1600_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: To attain the rank of Ayatollah and Marja-e Taqlid, a scholar must be granted this formal diploma certifying their mastery of independent legal derivation.
double_ayat_all_that_1600_a.explanation: Granted by senior masters in Najaf or Qom, an Ijaza certifies that the scholar possesses the capacity to deduce original Islamic rulings from the Quran and Sunnah.

double_ayat_all_that_2000_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The manual of Islamic jurisprudence published by every Grand Ayatollah as a practical guide for their followers is known by this Arabic title.
double_ayat_all_that_2000_a.explanation: The Risalah details rulings on prayer, fasting, business transactions, and purity, required reading for every practicing Shi'i follower (Muqallid).

double_ayat_all_that_400_b.clue_text: Before سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, this conservative Grand Ayatollah in Qom advocated political quietism and cooperation with the monarchy to protect the seminary from state persecution.
double_ayat_all_that_400_b.explanation: Golpayegani ran major hospitals, printing presses, and seminaries in Qom, serving as supreme traditionalist authority alongside Mar'ashi Najafi.

double_ayat_all_that_800_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The theological practice of dissimulating or concealing one's true religious convictions to save oneself from persecution or death is known as this.
double_ayat_all_that_800_b.explanation: Khomeini famously suspended Taqiyya during the سال ۱۳۴۲ خورشیدی protests, declaring: 'Taqiyya is forbidden when Islam itself is endangered!'

double_ayat_all_that_1200_b.clue_text: در سال ۱۳۵۹ خورشیدی, this veteran cleric and philosopher who drafted the Assembly of Experts constitution was chosen as the first Chief Justice of the Islamic Republic.
double_ayat_all_that_1200_b.explanation: Beheshti was killed on June 28, سال ۱۳۵۹ خورشیدی (7 Tir), alongside 72 senior officials when an MEK bomb destroyed the Islamic Republic Party headquarters.

double_ayat_all_that_1600_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The highest theological class in the Hawza curriculum, conducted as open seminars without textbooks where students debate master jurists, is known as this.
double_ayat_all_that_1600_b.explanation: Dars-e Kharij allows advanced scholars to present independent legal arguments, demonstrating their readiness to receive an Ijaza of Ijtihad.

double_ayat_all_that_2000_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Located in Qom, this historic theological library holds over 85,000 rare Islamic manuscripts, assembled by Grand Ayatollah Shahab al-Din Mar'ashi Najafi.
double_ayat_all_that_2000_b.explanation: Mar'ashi Najafi skipped meals and worked night shifts in Najaf bakeries in the 1920s to purchase manuscripts before European orientalists could acquire them.

double_shah_me_on_you_400_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The Shah's formidable twin sister who was nicknamed 'The Black Panther' by French journalists for her political assertiveness was named this.
double_shah_me_on_you_400_a.explanation: Ashraf met secretly with Kermit Roosevelt and General Norman Schwarzkopf Sr. in Paris در سال ۱۳۳۲ خورشیدی to convince her hesitant brother to back the coup against Mosaddegh.

double_shah_me_on_you_800_a.clue_text: Appointed Empress (Shahbanu) در سال ۱۳۴۶ خورشیدی and designated regent in case of the Shah's death, this third wife of the Shah was a patron of modern art and architecture.
double_shah_me_on_you_800_a.explanation: Farah Diba established the Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art در سال ۱۳۵۶ خورشیدی, acquiring masterpieces by Picasso, Warhol, Rothko, and Pollock.

double_shah_me_on_you_1200_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The Shah's exclusive winter retreat in the Swiss Alps, where he skied and conducted informal foreign diplomacy each January, was located in this luxury resort.
double_shah_me_on_you_1200_a.explanation: The Shah's month-long vacations at Villa Suvretta with kingpins and foreign journalists were heavily criticized during domestic economic crises.

double_shah_me_on_you_1600_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The elite 4,000-man bodyguard division tasked with protecting the royal family, who swore personal blood oaths to the Shah, was known as this.
double_shah_me_on_you_1600_a.explanation: Named after the ancient 10,000 Achaemenid Immortals, all candidates had to exceed six feet in height and undergo rigorous ideological screening.

double_shah_me_on_you_2000_a.clue_text: Between سال ۱۳۱۰ خورشیدی and سال ۱۳۱۵ خورشیدی, the young Crown Prince Mohammad Reza was sent by his father to attend this prestigious Swiss boarding school near Lake Geneva.
double_shah_me_on_you_2000_a.explanation: At Le Rosey, the future Shah befriended Western classmates like Prince Rainier of Monaco, developing fluent French and a lifelong passion for tennis and skiing.

double_shah_me_on_you_400_b.clue_text: The Shah's first marriage در سال ۱۳۱۸ خورشیدی was an arranged dynastic union uniting the Pahlavi monarchy with the royal house of this Arab kingdom.
double_shah_me_on_you_400_b.explanation: Reza Shah arranged the wedding with King Farouk's 17-year-old sister Princess Fawzia to boost Pahlavi international prestige.

double_shah_me_on_you_800_b.clue_text: در سال ۱۳۳۷ خورشیدی, the Shah divorced Queen Soraya Esfandiari Bakhtiari due to court dynastic pressure resulting from this personal tragedy.
double_shah_me_on_you_800_b.explanation: The سال ۱۲۸۵ خورشیدی Constitution required the crown prince to be born of an Iranian mother; after medical trips to American specialists proved fruitless, the Shah wept as he announced the divorce on radio.

double_shah_me_on_you_1200_b.clue_text: On October 26, سال ۱۳۴۶ خورشیدی, his 48th birthday, the Shah crowned himself at Golestan Palace and placed a custom Van Cleef & Arpels emerald tiara on this Empress.
double_shah_me_on_you_1200_b.explanation: She became the first woman crowned as Empress (Shahbanu) in Iranian history since the Sasanian queen Burandokht in the 7th century.

double_shah_me_on_you_1600_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The Shah held biannual planning conferences at this Caspian coastal resort in Mazandaran to dictate economic targets to his cabinet.
double_shah_me_on_you_1600_b.explanation: At the مرداد ۱۳۵۳ Ramsar conference, the Shah overruled economic planners and doubled the budget of the Fifth Plan, triggering ruinous inflation.

double_shah_me_on_you_2000_b.clue_text: The Shah's eldest son and designated heir, born in Tehran on October 31, سال ۱۳۳۹ خورشیدی, was named this.
double_shah_me_on_you_2000_b.explanation: His birth secured dynastic succession; thousands of prisoners were pardoned and free sugar was distributed to families across the nation.

double_opec_and_down_400_a.clue_text: Founded in Baghdad in شهریور ۱۳۳۹, Iran was one of the five founding members of OPEC alongside Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and this South American nation.
double_opec_and_down_400_a.explanation: Venezuelan oil minister Juan Pablo Pérez Alfonzo and Iranian delegates forged the cartel to counter unilateral price cuts by the 'Seven Sisters' Western oil majors.

double_opec_and_down_800_a.clue_text: Iran's chief OPEC representative who negotiated the historic سال ۱۳۵۲ خورشیدی price hikes and was later taken hostage by Carlos the Jackal in Vienna در سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی was named this.
double_opec_and_down_800_a.explanation: Amouzegar was held at gunpoint in Vienna alongside Saudi oil minister Sheikh Ahmed Zaki Yamani before being ransomed and flown to Algiers.

double_opec_and_down_1200_a.clue_text: On December 21, سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی, this Venezuelan Marxist terrorist stormed the OPEC ministerial conference in Vienna, taking 63 hostages including eleven oil ministers.
double_opec_and_down_1200_a.explanation: Carlos demanded the assassination of Yamani and Amouzegar, but was paid an estimated $20 to $50 million in ransom by Arab governments to release them in Algiers.

double_opec_and_down_1600_a.clue_text: در سال ۱۳۶۴ خورشیدی, during the Iran-Iraq War, Saudi Arabia flooded the global market with cheap oil to punish Iran, causing crude prices to crash to this historic low per barrel.
double_opec_and_down_1600_a.explanation: The price crash choked off Iran's foreign exchange earnings, making it impossible to purchase modern weapons and forcing Khomeini to accept UN Resolution 598 در سال ۱۳۶۷ خورشیدی.

double_opec_and_down_2000_a.clue_text: Headquartered initially in Geneva from سال ۱۳۳۹ خورشیدی to سال ۱۳۴۳ خورشیدی, OPEC relocated its permanent global secretariat to this neutral European capital city.
double_opec_and_down_2000_a.explanation: Austrian Chancellor Bruno Kreisky granted OPEC full extraterritorial diplomatic status in Vienna along the Danube Canal.

double_opec_and_down_400_b.clue_text: The international cartel of seven Anglo-American oil companies that controlled 85% of global crude reserves prior to the سال ۱۳۵۲ خورشیدی crisis was known by this moniker.
double_opec_and_down_400_b.explanation: Coined by Enrico Mattei of Italy's ENI, the Seven Sisters included BP, Shell, Exxon, Mobil, Chevron, Texaco, and Gulf Oil.

double_opec_and_down_800_b.clue_text: Under the سال ۱۳۳۳ خورشیدی Consortium Agreement signed after Mosaddegh's overthrow, British Petroleum retained this percentage share of Iranian oil production.
double_opec_and_down_800_b.explanation: American oil giants (Exxon, Mobil, Texaco, Socal, Gulf) received 40%, Shell took 14%, and CFP of France received 6%.

double_opec_and_down_1200_b.clue_text: در سال ۱۳۵۲ خورشیدی, the Shah declared that upon the expiration of the سال ۱۳۳۳ خورشیدی 25-year Consortium agreement در سال ۱۳۵۷ خورشیدی, Iran would do this with its oil industry.
options: Sell the oil fields to Saudi Arabia
double_opec_and_down_1200_b.explanation: The St. Moritz agreement of اردیبهشت ۱۳۵۲ transferred all operational management of the oil fields from the Western Consortium to NIOC.

double_opec_and_down_1600_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The massive petrochemical and refining complex on the Persian Gulf built as a 50-50 joint venture between Iran and Japan's Mitsui was known as this.
double_opec_and_down_1600_b.explanation: Heavily bombed during the Iran-Iraq War, Mitsui withdrew در سال ۱۳۶۸ خورشیدی after paying $1 billion in contract cancellation settlements.

double_opec_and_down_2000_b.clue_text: به دنبال سال ۱۳۵۲ خورشیدی quadrupling of oil prices, Iran became the world's fourth largest oil producer behind the US, USSR, and this Arab kingdom.
double_opec_and_down_2000_b.explanation: Iran pumped over six million barrels per day در سال ۱۳۵۳ خورشیدی, generating over $20 billion annually in foreign exchange reserves.

double_the_bombardment_chronicles_400_a.clue_text: On June 23, سال ۱۲۸۷ خورشیدی, this Tsarist Russian commander of the Persian Cossack Brigade directed artillery fire on the Baharestan Majles building.
double_the_bombardment_chronicles_400_a.explanation: Liakhov was appointed military governor of Tehran by Mohammad Ali Shah, establishing martial law and executing constitutionalist leaders.

double_the_bombardment_chronicles_800_a.clue_text: به دنبال سال ۱۲۸۷ خورشیدی bombardment, this fiery editor of the satirical newspaper Sur-e Esrafil was strangled in the gardens of Bagh-e Shah.
double_the_bombardment_chronicles_800_a.explanation: Before being strangled, Jahangir Khan boldly told his executioners: 'Long live the Constitution! Our blood will nourish the tree of liberty.'

double_the_bombardment_chronicles_1200_a.clue_text: The period of reactionary monarchical rule between the bombardment of the Majles in خرداد ۱۲۸۷ and the conquest of Tehran in تیر ۱۲۸۸ is called this.
double_the_bombardment_chronicles_1200_a.explanation: The eleven-month period ended when Bakhtiari tribesmen and Tabrizi fighters stormed Tehran and deposed Mohammad Ali Shah.

double_the_bombardment_chronicles_1600_a.clue_text: During the سال ۱۲۸۷ خورشیدی–سال ۱۲۸۸ خورشیدی royalist siege of Tabriz, this young American missionary and teacher was shot dead leading constitutionalist fighters.
double_the_bombardment_chronicles_1600_a.explanation: A Princeton graduate teaching at the Memorial School in Tabriz, Baskerville declared: 'I cannot stand by while these brave people fight for freedom.'

double_the_bombardment_chronicles_2000_a.clue_text: In تیر ۱۲۸۸, after constitutional forces captured Tehran, Mohammad Ali Shah fled his palace and took refuge in this foreign embassy in Zargandeh.
double_the_bombardment_chronicles_2000_a.explanation: The Grand National Assembly formally deposed the Shah and elevated his twelve-year-old son Ahmad Shah to the throne under a regency.

double_the_bombardment_chronicles_400_b.clue_text: The Armenian revolutionary commander who led the northern constitutionalist volunteer detachment that converged on Tehran in تیر ۱۲۸۸ was named this.
double_the_bombardment_chronicles_400_b.explanation: Yeprem Khan was appointed chief of police of Tehran, reorganizing the municipal gendarmerie and capturing royalist bastions.

double_the_bombardment_chronicles_800_b.clue_text: On July 31, سال ۱۲۸۸ خورشیدی, this prominent anti-constitutionalist high cleric was convicted of treason by a revolutionary tribunal and hanged in Toopkhaneh Square.
double_the_bombardment_chronicles_800_b.explanation: Nuri insisted that legislation must conform strictly to Islamic Shari'a (advocating Mashru'eh over Mashruteh), rejecting elected parliaments as apostasy.

double_the_bombardment_chronicles_1200_b.clue_text: In بهمن ۱۲۸۷, this revolutionary electrical engineer threw two homemade hand bombs at Mohammad Ali Shah's motorized carriage near Do-Shan Tappeh.
double_the_bombardment_chronicles_1200_b.explanation: The bomb killed several royal outriders and horses, but the Shah survived unhurt inside an armored carriage.

double_the_bombardment_chronicles_1600_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The military park in central Tehran where Mohammad Ali Shah established his military command tent and tortured captured constitutionalists was known as this.
double_the_bombardment_chronicles_1600_b.explanation: Prisoners were held in heavy iron neck-chains in the garden, with royalists mocking them before summary executions.

double_the_bombardment_chronicles_2000_b.clue_text: Following his deposition, Mohammad Ali Shah launched an ill-fated armed invasion در سال ۱۲۹۰ خورشیدی to reclaim his throne, landing on the Caspian coast from this country.
double_the_bombardment_chronicles_2000_b.explanation: Funded by Russian loans, the ex-Shah landed at Gomshaneh with Turkmen tribal cavalry, but was routed by government forces under Yeprem Khan and Sardar As'ad.

double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_400_a.clue_text: In خرداد ۱۳۳۱, Dr. Mohammad Mosaddegh traveled to this Dutch city to personally defend Iran's sovereign right to nationalize oil before the World Court.
double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_400_a.explanation: The court ruled 9-to-5 that it lacked jurisdiction over the dispute, handing Mosaddegh a triumphant international legal victory over the British Empire.

double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_800_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: During cabinet meetings and foreign diplomatic summits with Averell Harriman, Mosaddegh famously conducted high-stakes state business while wearing these clothes in bed.
double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_800_a.explanation: Western reporters coined the term 'pajama diplomacy' as Mosaddegh exploited his genuine fainting spells and frailty to disarm hardline negotiators.

double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_1200_a.clue_text: On ۳۰ تیر ۱۳۳۱ (30 Tir 1331), nationwide mass strikes and bloody clashes in Baharestan Square forced the Shah to dismiss this short-lived British-backed Prime Minister.
double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_1200_a.explanation: Qavam held office for barely four days, issuing a radio threat to 'steer the ship of state with an iron hand' before popular fury forced his flight.

double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_1600_a.clue_text: Following his overthrow in مرداد ۱۳۳۲, Mosaddegh was tried by a military tribunal for high treason and sentenced to this punishment.
double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_1600_a.explanation: Mosaddegh was confined under armed SAVAK guard at his private ancestral fortress in Ahmadabad-e Mosaddegh until his death on March 5, سال ۱۳۴۶ خورشیدی.

double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_2000_a.clue_text: Mosaddegh earned his doctorate in law در سال ۱۲۹۳ خورشیدی from this Swiss university, making him the first Iranian to earn a European doctoral degree in jurisprudence.
double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_2000_a.explanation: His dissertation examined Islamic wills and testamentary succession in Shi'i jurisprudence.

double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_400_b.clue_text: In مهر ۱۳۳۰, Dr. Mosaddegh traveled to New York to address this United Nations body, denouncing British naval blockades of Iranian oil tankers.
double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_400_b.explanation: Britain introduced a resolution demanding enforcement of ICJ interim measures, but Mosaddegh rallied non-aligned nations, forcing the council to adjourn without a vote.

double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_800_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The British secret intelligence operation to topple Dr. Mosaddegh, codenamed by MI6 alongside the CIA's Operation Ajax, was named this.
double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_800_b.explanation: Devised by British spy Monty Woodhouse, it was merged into the joint Anglo-American coup plan authorized by Churchill and Eisenhower.

double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_1200_b.clue_text: Mosaddegh's courageous, uncompromising Foreign Minister who evaded arrest for months before being captured, stabbed by royalists, and executed by firing squad در سال ۱۳۳۳ خورشیدی was named this.
double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_1200_b.explanation: Fatemi was editor of the radical daily Bakhtar-e Emruz; he was shot on November 10, سال ۱۳۳۳ خورشیدی, shouting 'Long live Iran! Long live Mosaddegh!'

double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_1600_b.clue_text: In مرداد ۱۳۳۲, Mosaddegh held a controversial nationwide referendum using separate ballot booths for 'Yes' and 'No' voters to dissolve this body.
double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_1600_b.explanation: The dissolution of parliament provided the legal pretext used by royalists and the CIA to argue that the Shah had the constitutional right to dismiss the Prime Minister.

double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_2000_b.clue_text: On March 5, سال ۱۳۴۶ خورشیدی, Dr. Mosaddegh died at age 84 at his country estate in Ahmadabad, his request to be buried alongside the martyrs of this سال ۱۳۳۱ خورشیدی uprising denied by the Shah.
double_mossad_egh_in_the_middle_2000_b.explanation: Mosaddegh was buried beneath the floorboards of his private dining room at Ahmadabad, where his body remains to this day.

double_tahrir_ic_vocals_400_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The rapid vocal ornamentation and melodic yodeling produced in the upper throat and falsetto characteristic of Persian classical singing is called this.
double_tahrir_ic_vocals_400_a.explanation: Tahrir is often compared to a nightingale's warble, requiring decades of vocal diaphragm and throat control.

double_tahrir_ic_vocals_800_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Universally revered as 'Khosrow-ye Avaz-e Iran' (The Emperor of Iranian Song), this Khorasani master vocalist recorded the iconic protest anthem Morgh-e Sahar.
double_tahrir_ic_vocals_800_a.explanation: Shajarian was awarded the UNESCO Mozart Medal and taught generations of classical singers before his death در سال ۱۳۹۹ خورشیدی.

double_tahrir_ic_vocals_1200_a.clue_text: Famed for singing the patriotic anthem 'Ey Iran' and wearing dark horn-rimmed glasses after losing an eye in a سال ۱۳۲۹ خورشیدی car crash, this singer had a velvet baritone voice.
double_tahrir_ic_vocals_1200_a.explanation: Banan revolutionized Persian vocal style by abandoning loud shouting in favor of intimate, whispered microphone phrasing on Radio Tehran's Golha programs.

double_tahrir_ic_vocals_1600_a.clue_text: The premier cultural radio broadcast founded در سال ۱۳۳۵ خورشیدی by Davood Pirnia that introduced Persian classical poetry to millions of listeners was called this.
double_tahrir_ic_vocals_1600_a.explanation: Golha produced over 1,500 episodes under categories like Golha-ye Javidan, Golha-ye Rang-a-Rang, and Yek Shakheh Gol.

double_tahrir_ic_vocals_2000_a.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: This preeminent female classical vocalist, famed as 'Banu-ye Avaz-e Iran' (The Lady of Iranian Song), collaborated closely with composers Homayoun Khorram and Parviz Yahaqi.
double_tahrir_ic_vocals_2000_a.explanation: Marzieh was the first female singer to perform on Radio Tehran's prestigious Golha-ye Rang-a-Rang programs.

double_tahrir_ic_vocals_400_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The primary mode (Dastgah) of Persian classical music, representing serenity and mystical passion and forming the parent modal root of Abu-Ata, Dashti, and Afshari, is this.
double_tahrir_ic_vocals_400_b.explanation: Shur is considered the mother of all twelve Persian Dastgahs, its Koron microtonal flat intervals evoking deep longing.

double_tahrir_ic_vocals_800_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The son of Ostad Mohammad Reza Shajarian, renowned for his breath control and hit classical fusion albums like Neither Angel Nor Devil, is named this.
double_tahrir_ic_vocals_800_b.explanation: Homayoun began as a tombak player accompanying his father before emerging as one of the most commercially successful vocalists in modern Iran.

double_tahrir_ic_vocals_1200_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: Known as the 'Knight of Persian Song', this Kermanshahi master vocalist was the first to set the mystical poetry of Jalal al-Din Rumi to epic Kurdish and Persian rhythms.
double_tahrir_ic_vocals_1200_b.explanation: His سال ۱۳۶۲ خورشیدی album Yadegar-e Doost, composed by Kambiz Roshanravan to mark Rumi's anniversary, was the bestselling classical cassette in Iranian history.

double_tahrir_ic_vocals_1600_b.clue_text: این سرنخ تاریخی: The non-metric, rhythmically free vocal section where a singer improvises classical poetry accompanied by a single solo instrument (like tar, ney, or kamancheh) is called this.
double_tahrir_ic_vocals_1600_b.explanation: Avaz is the true test of a Persian vocalist's mastery, demanding improvised transitions through various melodic Gushehs according to the poetic meter.

double_tahrir_ic_vocals_2000_b.clue_text: The microtonal pitch alteration in Persian classical music that lowers a musical note by approximately a quarter-tone (roughly 30 to ۶۰ میلادیnts) is named this.
double_tahrir_ic_vocals_2000_b.explanation: Pioneered in modern notation by Ostad Ali-Naqi Vaziri در سال ۱۳۰۲ خورشیدی, Koron lowers a note by a quarter-tone, while Sori raises it by a quarter-tone.

double_crown_jewels_and_crowd_jeers_400_.clue_text: Carved with the names of Mughal emperors Akbar and Jahangir before being seized by Nader Shah, this 88-carat yellow diamond was given to Tsar Nicholas I در سال ۱۲۰۷ خورشیدی.
double_crown_jewels_and_crowd_jeers_400_.explanation: Prince Khosrow Mirza delivered the Shah Diamond to St. Petersburg as royal blood money to apologize for the murder of diplomat Alexander Griboyedov.

double_crown_jewels_and_crowd_jeers_800_.clue_text: Fabricated by Paris jeweler Van Cleef & Arpels for the سال ۱۳۴۶ خورشیدی coronation of Empress Farah, her platinum crown featured this many carats of emeralds and diamonds.
